articles.title: Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy Set To Make Season Debut Against Arkansas
articles.summary: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy, who suffered a gunshot wound this offseason, will make his season debut Saturday against Arkansas.
articles.body: After an offseason gunshot wound, questions swirled around whether Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy would see the field again this season. On Thursday afternoon, Hardy and the Tigers got their answer. According to a report from ESPN, Hardy will make his season debut on Saturday for the Tigers against the Arkansas Razorbacks. While Hardy isn't expected to start the game, he is still in line to handle a handful of carries. Running back Jamal Roberts will keep his starting role while the Tigers gradually integrate Hardy back into the mix. Together, they give Missouri one of the most formidable backfields in college football. After transferring from UL Monroe in 2024, Hardy made a seamless transition into the SEC. He quickly established himself as one of the premier running backs in college football and a top prospect for the 2027 NFL Draft. Last season, Hardy carried the ball 256 times for 1,649 yards (6.4 yards per carry) and 16 touchdowns. He rushed for 300 yards and three touchdowns in a 49-27 win over Mississippi State. It remains unclear whether Hardy will declare for the NFL Draft or return for another season, despite being projected as a top running back with a potential first-round grade. Following his recovery, returning to school for another year could offer him a full season to improve his draft stock. The good news is Hardy has plenty of time to make that decision, as he still has two years of eligibility remaining. With his return to the field this weekend, all eyes will be on how long it takes Hardy to break off one of the signature long runs we've come to expect from him. Simply making it back onto the field this season is an incredible accomplishment for one of the sport's premier running backs.

articles.title: Coaching Changes That Will Impact The 2026-27 Men's College Basketball Season
articles.summary: Here's a look at the coaching changes that could have a major impact on the 2026-27 men's college basketball season.
articles.body: The college basketball coaching carousel was active this offseason. Will Wade is back at LSU. Michael Malone is bringing NBA championship pedigree to a blue blood. The reigning national champion, Michigan, lost its coach to the pros. And several other top programs are putting their trust in former mid-major coaches. Those moves will have a major impact on the 2026-27 season. Here's a look at the coaching changes that could matter most. Will Wade (NC State → LSU) Will Wade is back in Baton Rouge, returning to the program where he previously coached from 2017-22. LSU fired Wade in 2022 following a series of NCAA violations, and after a brief stint away from coaching, he rebuilt his career at McNeese (2023-25) before spending one season at NC State. When former LSU coach Matt McMahon was fired, Wade got the call to return. This offseason, Wade assembled a roster loaded with transfers and fifth-year players who needed lawsuits to obtain eligibility, including stars Donovan Dent and RJ Luis. Michael Malone (NBA → North Carolina) Following Hubert Davis' firing in March, North Carolina turned to NBA coaching talent, hiring Michael Malone to lead the Tar Heels. The Denver Nuggets parted ways with Malone after the 2025 NBA season, and he spent the following year as an NBA broadcaster. Now, Malone begins his first stint as a college head coach, bringing more than 10 seasons of NBA coaching experience — including a 2023 NBA championship with Denver — to one of college basketball's most storied programs. Malone enters his debut season hoping to bring the Tar Heels back to national prominence. Mike Boynton Jr. (Promoted) Dusty May was poached by the Dallas Mavericks after leading Michigan to a national championship. Assistant Mike Boynton Jr. was promoted to interim head coach, and eventually signed a two-year deal with the program in July. He retained all but one player — L.J. Cason — during the NCAA-mandated transfer portal window following a coaching change. Before being hired as an assistant at Michigan, Boynton was the head coach at Oklahoma State for seven seasons, where he went 119-109, making one NCAA Tournament appearance. Now, after two seasons as an assistant, Boynton will guide a Wolverines team that lost its top three players to the NBA Draft. Tony Stubblefield (Promoted) Tony Stubblefield was promoted to interim head coach after Dana Altman announced his retirement. In his 11 seasons on Oregon's staff, Stubblefield has been part of eight NCAA Tournaments, including five Sweet 16s, two Elite Eights and a Final Four appearance. Stubblefield left the program for a brief stint as DePaul's head coach, where he went 30-66 from 2021-2024, but was let go midway through the 2024 season. The coaching change opened a transfer portal window for Oregon's players, but with the season fast approaching, no one has elected to leave. Randy Bennett (St. Mary's → Arizona State) Randy Bennett is back in his home state as he enters his first season leading the Sun Devils. He brings an impressive résumé to Arizona State, including 25 seasons as Saint Mary's head coach, 12 NCAA Tournament appearances and seven West Coast Conference regular-season titles. After the Sun Devils went 17-16 last season, Bennett will look to get ASU back to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2023. He replaces Bobby Hurley, who spent 11 seasons as the program's head coach. Jerrod Calhoun (Utah State → Cincinnati) Jerrod Calhoun joined the Big 12 to lead the Cincinnati Bearcats, returning to his alma mater after two seasons at Utah State. Calhoun led the Aggies to a 55-15 record and back-to-back NCAA Tournament appearances during his tenure. Now, he'll look to bring that success to Cincinnati after replacing former Bearcats coach Wes Miller. Meanwhile, former Northern Iowa coach Ben Jacobson takes over for Calhoun at Utah State. Bryan Hodgson (South Florida → Providence) Bryan Hodgson took over at Providence following an underwhelming 15-18 finish last year. He joined the Friars after one season at South Florida, where he led the Bulls to an impressive 25-9 record and an NCAA Tournament appearance. Now tasked with building a roster largely composed of transfers, Hodgson will look to return Providence to the postseason for the first time in three seasons. He also beat out several high-major programs and blue bloods to secure a commitment from 2027 recruit Lewis Uwvo, the No. 7-ranked player in the 247Sports rankings. Gerry McNamara (Siena → Syracuse) A familiar face returns to Syracuse as Gerry McNamara will begin his first season as head coach of the Orange. McNamara played guard for Syracuse from 2002-06. He started 135 games in college, and averaged 35 minutes per game as a freshman on Syracuse's national championship team with Carmelo Anthony. McNamara returned to his former school after two seasons at Siena, where he won a MAAC conference title and led the team to an NCAA Tournament appearance. Justin Gainey (Tennessee → NC State) Justin Gainey has returned to NC State, this time as the Wolfpack's head coach. He played for the program from 1996-2000 before joining Rick Barnes' staff at Tennessee as an assistant. Now, after Will Wade's departure for LSU, Gainey will look to lead his alma mater back to the NCAA Tournament. Casey Alexander (Belmont → Kansas State) After parting ways with former head coach Jerome Tang, who led Kansas State to an Elite Eight, the Wildcats brought in Casey Alexander ahead of the 2026-27 season. Alexander spent the past seven seasons at Belmont, where he recorded seven consecutive 20-win seasons and compiled a 166-60 record. A former Belmont guard (1991-95), Alexander takes over a Wildcats team coming off a disappointing 12-20 season and will look to get the program back to the postseason.

articles.title: Tom Brady Wonders If Defenders Are Being Treated Fairly On Roughing The Passer Calls
articles.summary: Tom Brady wants officials to give defenses some grace when it comes to hitting the quarterback.
articles.body: Yes, Tom Brady understands the irony behind his disagreements with the roughing-the-passer penalties called in Sunday's Green Bay Packers-Detroit Lions game. That won't stop him from advocating for defensive players to get some more leeway when it comes to hitting quarterbacks, though. In the most recent edition of #AskTom, Brady said that quarterbacks should take some more accountability on certain hits, adding that it comes with the territory of playing the position. "On the field, I just think there's a level of aggressiveness that the defenders need to play with in order to do their job well — whether that's rushing the passer or closing on a receiver to knock the ball off them. I just think sometimes we're calling it a little too close," Brady said. "The quarterbacks, they have every right to get rid of the ball whenever they want. The faster they get that ball out of their hands, the less likely they are to get hit. "But if they want to hold the ball, part of the understanding is that you're gonna get hit." There were a handful of penalties that Brady expressed his displeasure with when he was on the call for the Packers-Lions game on FOX. When Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes hit Packers running back Marshawn Lloyd on a pass thrown his way and was called for unnecessary roughness, Brady blurted, "Oh, come on, man." "That’s allowed 99 out of 100 … it’s a bang-bang play," Brady added of the penalty called on Barnes at the time. The one that seemed to irk Brady the most, though, was the roughing the passer that was called on Packers defensive tackle Karl Brooks for his hit on Jared Goff during the Lions' final drive. It appeared that Brooks hit Goff in a split second after he threw it. "No, my goodness, what is that? There’s no way," Brady said of the penalty on Sunday's broadcast. "Brooks on the tackle kind of makes a great play. It’s a bang-bang play. He rolls off his body; it’s a great throw by Goff, that’s definitely not roughing the passer. "You’re just ripping through the line of scrimmage to try to get the quarterback on the ground," Brady continued. "Look, I love Goff standing there in the pocket, but you just can’t tack it on 15 yards." FOX Sports NFL rules analyst Dean Blandino agreed with Brady's assessment of the penalty, saying that Brooks' hit "wasn't late." That penalty helped Detroit get deep into Green Bay territory, allowing it to kick the game-winning field goal as time expired, which led Brady to call the penalty "a little bit controversial" on #AskTom. And as Brady criticized the officiating for calling roughing the passer penalties he thought were weak, he admitted that it's easier for him to feel that way now that he's retired. "Look, I understand. I'm self-aware," Brady said as some on social media thought he was a bit hypocritical for him to call out the officiating. "I'm sitting up in that booth. It's much easier for me to say it now that I'm sitting up in the booth, but that's what my job is. I'm a broadcaster now, right? I have these types of opinions." Brady's thoughts on some controversial penalty calls weren't the only thing that went viral from his call during Sunday's Packers-Lions game. When it appeared the Lions were going to pass the ball on one of the final plays from scrimmage, Brady blurted, "Don't tell me they're going to throw this? Oh my God, they're going to throw this." The Lions ended up running the ball on the ensuing play, which allowed them to bleed some more clock before kicking the game-winning field goal. But when Brady was asked about that call and the Lions' unsuccessful fourth-down attempt from deep in their own territory on #AskTom, he still shared some anxiety he had in those moments. "At that part, I did," Brady said when asked if he ever forgets that he's on a broadcast seen by millions of people. "After a while, you start thinking, 'Am I the one that is seeing this the wrong way? Did they just go for it in a tie game on their own 20-yard line? Is that what happened with the line? And they didn't get it? Oh my God.' "When you're not in on every thought or conversation going on those coaching headsets, a lot of these times, I'm just trying to speak out loud what exactly I'm seeing." And Brady thinks that the Lions might have gotten a bit lucky in their win over the Packers. "Look, I know they're an aggressive fourth-down team, but maybe the football Gods were looking after them a little bit this last Sunday, let's be honest," Brady said. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. articles.title: Jordan Love For MVP? 3 Takeaways From Packers' Win Over Panthers
articles.summary: Jordan Love should be considered an MVP candidate is among the things we learned from the Packers' win over the Panthers.
articles.body: It’s crazy to think that Micah Parsons hasn’t even played a snap yet for the Green Bay Packers, because they’re starting to look pretty darn good without him. They beat the Carolina Panthers, 27-13, on Thursday night at Lambeau Field. There were warts. There were issues — particularly in the fourth quarter. But the Packers held on. And it must not feel great that the Packers entered this week as the fourth-ranked team in the NFC North — and the Panthers entered this week first in the NFC South. This helped demonstrate the substantial divide in quality between the two divisions. But there’s no consolation for the Packers, who face a tough schedule to get themselves into the playoffs. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves: thinking about the playoffs. Here are my takeaways from the Packers' win over the Panthers: 1.Jordan Love Has A Legit Shot At MVP The Packers QB is earning a reputation for the way he throws the deep ball. It’s magic to watch him heave the ball in the direction of Christian Watson. Then Matthew Golden. Then Savion Williams or J. Michael Sturdivant. Whoever, really. Doesn’t matter. But that might not even be the most impressive part of his game. My favorite element of Love’s game is the way he can beat the beat. It’s a beautiful thing. Against the Panthers’ relentless blitzes, Love finished 15 of 19 for 130 yards and two touchdowns. Love is making himself more and more valuable to the Packers with every game — compensating for the lack of rushing efficiency. (More on that later.) This is an important element of an MVP candidacy. You have to face adversity. You have to win a lot of games and make the playoffs — but you also have to overcome severe obstacles. This putrid run game qualifies. Their decision to throw on third-and-2 for a first down in the fourth quarter spoke to Love’s MVP status, at least for the Packers. (It also spoke to their lack of faith in the run game.) It should be a tough and tight MVP race this year, from Josh Allen to Joe Burrow to Caleb Williams. But Love has inserted himself into the conversation. He’s going to rack up wins. He’s going to rack up stats. His highlights are going to be absurd. What’s not to like? 2.Bryce Young Can't Handle The Pressure — And He's Getting Further Away From Big Extension This is the second consecutive week where pressure has rendered Young useless. We saw in the early season that Young can be an effective pocket passer when given the requisite time to throw. But if you were like me, you saw the Browns game (when he really struggled on third and fourth downs) and you saw a harbinger that things could get bad — in a hurry — for Young. And now they have. This week, against the blitz, he was 6 of 13 for 68 yards, one touchdown and one interception with a completion percentage over expected of -10.9%. And against pressure, he was 7 of 17 for 41 yards and an interception for 2.4 yards per attempt. Every QB is bad against pressure. It’s one of the few rules in football that you can count on. But as I just mentioned in praising Love, the best quarterbacks can beat the blitz. They knew where to go with the ball. They know how to get the ball out of their hands before the blitz arrives. So can Young be one of those QBs? For most of the game, he looked totally stumped by what Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon dialed up. There was really only one drive — the touchdown drive to Jalen Coker — where Young showed promise in beating the blitz. And to Young’s credit, he might be contending with the worst left tackle in football, Rasheed Walker. He allowed seven pressures, one sack and took two penalties. The Panthers have stuck with Young through thick and thin — working toward his development. And they deserve credit for that. But there’s something called the sunk cost fallacy, an irrational tendency to continue an endeavor or relationship after investing time and money — even when it makes more sense to move on. With Young, the Panthers will have to battle that. But nights like Thursday make me wonder if the Panthers might have a new QB in 2027. 3.Christian Watson Is Suddenly The Biggest Iron Man Of All Time In the first half, Watson caught a 52-yarder, but Panthers cornerback Will Lee landed on the receiver after he went to the ground. They both writhed in pain and headed to the locker room — and Watson eventually left the stadium in an ambulance to check out his chest injury at a local hospital. His night was over. Like, totally over. It had to be, because no one would get back in the game after going to the hospital. This isn’t pro wrestling. Right? Yes, Watson returned to Lambeau Field in an ambulance. And yes, he got back into the game, where he managed to snag one more catch for six yards. This defies most things we know about injuries — and ambulance rides. But it also defies what I thought I knew about Watson. He has missed a game in every season since he entered the NFL in 2022. It was the biggest inhibiting factor in him taking a major leap into WR1 status. But here he was, suffering a chest injury (and making a hospital trip) — before returning to the game. You can question whether this was a smart or sensible idea. But you can’t question Watson’s toughness. He’s suddenly an Iron Man. 3 1/2. What's Next? The Packers get to use their mini bye in preparation for the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium next week. That should be a big one for the folks in New England, where they’ll be celebrating Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction — and Tom Brady’s first return to Foxborough as a broadcaster. Green Bay gets a chance to play spoiler. The Packers can keep building off this performance. Maybe they’ll even figure out how to run the football. The Panthers will host the Denver Broncos at Bank of America Stadium next weekend. And if the Panthers thought the Packers defense was a tough opponent, they’ll be disappointed to hear that the Broncos have been even better — allowing the seventh-fewest points per game. It’s not exactly a get-right opportunity. The Panthers will have to hope they can hold up better against the blitz. And it seems like it might be a bad moment to take on Denver, with Broncos QB Bo Nix showing signs of improvement after a horrific run of four weeks. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Why did Elliotte Friedman say the Detroit Red Wings and San Jose Sharks discussed Simon Edvinsson “pretty deeply” amid NHL trade rumors
articles.summary: NHL insider Elliotte Friedman discusses the ongoing trade rumors involving Simon Edvinsson as the Detroit Red Wings and San Jose Sharks engage in significant talks. With the December 1 contract deadline approaching, find out Detroit's position and why the Sharks are considered potential suitors for the young defenseman.
articles.body: The Detroit Red Wings and San Jose Sharks have held significant discussions about defenseman Simon Edvinsson, according to NHL insider Elliotte Friedman. His latest comments have placed San Jose among the potential destinations for the unsigned restricted free agent, although a trade is far from certain.Detroit interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has previously expressed a clear desire to retain Edvinsson, while the December 1 contract deadline adds urgency to the situation.What Elliotte Friedman revealed about Simon Edvinsson’s NHL trade talksElliotte Friedman confirmed that the Detroit Red Wings and San Jose Sharks have discussed Simon Edvinsson extensively, but he did not indicate that a deal was close.Speaking on Thursday's edition of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast, Friedman said the two teams had talked about Edvinsson “pretty deeply.” He also made it clear that the discussions did not guarantee a trade.“I do think that the Red Wings and the Sharks have talked about Edvinsson pretty deeply,” Friedman said.The insider added that he was unsure what San Jose was prepared to offer or whether the conversations would lead to an agreement. His comments, shared by Rinky Report on X, nevertheless identified the Sharks as a potential destination for the 23-year-old defenseman.What is Detroit’s position on Simon Edvinsson?Detroit has publicly indicated that it would prefer to keep Edvinsson rather than move him. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff made that position clear on October 14.“I have zero interest in trading Simon Edvinsson, I want to keep him,” Horcoff said, according to The Detroit Free Press reporter Helene St. James.Edvinsson was selected sixth overall by Detroit in the 2021 NHL Draft. He recorded nine goals and 25 points in 72 games during the 2025-26 season, finishing with a plus-12 rating, and his average ice time of 22:21 ranked second among Red Wings skaters, behind Moritz Seider.His importance to Detroit’s defense would make a potential departure huge. Especially as the team is still evaluating its roster.Why could the December 1 deadline affect trade talks?Edvinsson remains unsigned after completing his entry-level contract, and according to the supplied report, he must sign an NHL contract by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 to remain eligible to play during the 2026-27 season. Any team acquiring his rights would face the same deadline.That leaves Detroit with a limited window to resolve the contract situation. If negotiations remain unsuccessful, the Red Wings could consider whether a trade offers a better outcome than having the defenseman remain unavailable.San Jose also has reasons to explore the possibility. The Sharks are building around young forwards Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and Michael Misa, and adding a top-pairing left-shot defenseman could address an important roster need.However, no specific offer from San Jose has been publicly confirmed. The Boston Bruins have also been mentioned among the teams involved in discussions, while reports have suggested that as many as 10 clubs could have explored Edvinsson's availability.For now, the Detroit Red Wings' preference to retain Simon Edvinsson remains clear; whether the San Jose Sharks are willing to make an offer compelling enough to change that position is the central question surrounding these NHL trade rumors.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Connor McDavid said Tristan Jarry “played great” after Edmonton Oilers defeated Calgary Flames 4-0 in their NHL Battle of Alberta match
articles.summary: In a recent NHL matchup, Connor McDavid commended Tristan Jarry for his outstanding goaltending performance in the Edmonton Oilers' 4-0 victory over the Calgary Flames, marking Jarry's first shutout of the season and a crucial win for the team.
articles.body: Connor McDavid praised Tristan Jarry after the Edmonton Oilers goalie stopped all 24 shots in a 4-0 victory over the Calgary Flames. Jarry delivered his first shutout of the season, making several important saves to help Edmonton secure another win in the Battle of Alberta.McDavid said Jarry’s composure and ability to handle pressure, especially in the first period and second period, was a big reason why. The Oilers captain also expressed confidence in Edmonton’s goaltending options, emphasizing the importance of having multiple capable players available.Connor McDavid praises Tristan Jarry after Edmonton Oilers’ NHL shutoutConnor McDavid described Tristan Jarry’s display as excellent, highlighting the saves that helped the Edmonton Oilers maintain their advantage against the Calgary Flames.“I thought he played great,” McDavid said after the game. “He made some big saves, especially early in the game and in the second period there. He was really, really solid.”The Edmonton captain's comments recognized Jarry's contribution beyond the final score. The goaltender faced 24 shots and prevented Calgary from finding a way onto the scoreboard, giving the Oilers a strong foundation for their 4-0 result.McDavid also addressed the team's depth in goal, saying Edmonton had three capable options and believed each could allow the team to win, and his remarks reflected the importance of maintaining confidence in the available goaltenders rather than relying on a single player.Tristan Jarry's goalie skills helped the Edmonton Oilers to a winJarry produced a 24-save shutout, making it his first of the 2026-27 season and the 24th of his NHL career. The result also moved his record to 3-1-2.The Oilers established control through goals from Mathieu Joseph, Mattias Ekholm, Kasperi Kapanen and Alex Formenton. Joseph opened the scoring at 7:26 of the first period after receiving a pass from McDavid. Ekholm doubled the advantage early in the second period.Kapanen then converted a power-play opportunity just 55 seconds into the third period. Formenton added another goal only 21 seconds later, giving Edmonton a four-goal cushion.Jarry acknowledged the defensive effort in front of him when discussing the shutout.“I think any time you can blank the board like that, it also gives credit to the team in front,” he said, adding that the Oilers did a good job of keeping Calgary's opportunities to the outside.What does the shutout mean for Edmonton Oilers and Calgary Flames?The victory improved Edmonton's record to 9-2-2, further strengthening its position during the early part of the NHL season. Calgary, meanwhile, saw its four-game winning streak come to an end.McDavid contributed two assists, extending his season-opening point streak to 13 games and taking his league-leading points total to 36. His continued production, combined with Jarry's performance, gave Edmonton another encouraging result.Jarry’s shutout was especially big following a rough stretch in Edmonton. Acquired from the Pittsburgh Penguins in a trade involving Stuart Skinner back in December 2025, he had struggled to find consistency in his earlier appearances, posting a 3.86 goals-against average and .858 save percentage in his prior Edmonton stint, eventually losing the starting role to Connor Ingram.The Oilers are managing their goaltending options and Jarry's last outing was a fortunate reminder of the depth the coaching staff has at its disposal, and McDavid's public support did nothing to hurt the team's confidence in its goaltenders.The loss was a reminder for Calgary of the difficulty of cracking a disciplined defense and the Flames will need to rebound after seeing their winning streak snapped. The Oilers can draw confidence from a win that combined effective scoring with reliable goaltending.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chase sparks Bangladesh collapse as West Indies on top in Mirpur Test
articles.summary: West Indies’ Royston Chase forces collapse as Bangladesh slump to 79-6, a lead of 106 runs, on day three of first Test.
articles.body:
Skipper Roston Chase claimed 3-25 and kept alive the West Indies’ hopes of beating Bangladesh after three days of the first cricket Test .

Chase’s off-spin was instrumental in triggering a collapse as Bangladesh slumped to 79-6 and a lead of 106 runs in the second innings at stumps, which came early due to bad light.

Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican, who had figures of 5-53 in the first innings, took 2-19 to complement his captain.

“Whatever score they give us tomorrow, we are going to chase it down,” West Indies batting coach Floyd Reifer said.

“It is unfortunate that we didn’t get past their total, but it was a great effort from the guys to come back and have Bangladesh at 79-6. We bowled in disciplined areas, stuck to our team plans and everyone really hustled out there in the heat.”

The West Indies conceded a 27-run first-innings lead and pace bowler Shamar Joseph struck in the second over of Bangladesh’s reply, dismissing opener Tanzid Hasan for a duck.

Chase then removed Shadman Islam, the centurion in the first innings , for 13 and Towhid Hridoy for 2 in the space of three balls.

Then Chase took out counterpart Najmul Hossain Shanto on 10. Warrican sent back Liton Das, trapping him lbw for 4, leaving Bangladesh at 35-5.

Warrican also broke the brief resistance of Mehidy Hasan Miraz by rattling his stump on 9 as Bangladesh were reduced to 53-6.

Jaker Ali and Nayeem Hasan were batting on 18 runs each when play was called off.

“We will try to score as many runs as possible,” Nayeem said. “Jaker bhai and I are batting now. If we can bat for a long time it will be good for us. Even 200 runs would be a very good total, but we will try to score more.”

Jaker came into the side as a concussion substitute for Mominul Haque, who received a blow on his head while fielding at short leg.

Nayeem earlier returned figures of 4-33 with his off-spin to bowl West Indies out for 245 after the visitors resumed the day at 134-4.

Tagenarine Chanderpaul’s stubbornness earned him his third half-century from 164 balls when he flicked Taijul Islam for a single.

However, soon after his laborious 50 he edged a delivery off pacer Shoriful Islam to second slip, ending a 65-run partnership with Justin Greaves for the fifth wicket.

Chanderpaul played 184 balls for 56 runs that included six fours and one six.

After Chanderpaul’s departure, Greaves and Chase looked solid in the crease as they took the side past 200 runs.

But Nayeem dismissed Greaves on 46 and followed with the wickets of Shamar Joseph and Warrican to confirm Bangladesh’s lead on the first innings . Chase was stranded on 43.

Bangladesh were bowled out for 272 in their first innings.

articles.title: Randy Orton’s tattoos and their meanings in 2026: How the WWE legend’s distinctive body art reflects his personal growth, family tributes, faith, and evolution into The Viper
articles.summary: Discover the meanings behind Randy Orton's tattoos in 2026, illustrating his personal journey, family tributes, and evolution into The Viper, along with legal disputes over their depiction in WWE games.
articles.body: Randy Orton has spent more than two decades establishing himself as one of WWE’s most recognisable performers. Known as The Viper, the veteran wrestler is associated with his calculated in-ring style, signature RKO and distinctive appearance, and his tattoos have become an important part of that image, evolving alongside his character and career.However, Orton’s body art tells a story beyond professional wrestling, and his designs include references to his family, religious beliefs and personal experiences, while the development of his tattoo collection reflects changes in his public persona. The artwork has also attracted attention outside the ring, particularly through a copyright dispute involving the reproduction of his tattoos in WWE video games.What Randy Orton’s WWE tattoos reveal about his lifeOrton’s tattoos developed over several stages of his wrestling career, beginning with tribal-inspired designs and expanding into larger pieces across his arms and back, and the artwork helped establish a distinctive visual identity that audiences could recognise immediately, whether he was competing in the ring, appearing on television or promoting WWE events.Some of his earliest designs reflected the tattoo styles popular during his early wrestling years. The tribal artwork across his upper back became one of the defining elements of his appearance, while additional designs gradually covered his arms. Over time, these pieces developed into a more extensive collection featuring skulls, religious imagery and personal symbols.Orton’s time in the United States Marine Corps also forms part of the background to his tattoo history. He previously had a USMC tattoo on his arm, but the design was later covered. His military service ended with a bad-conduct discharge after he went absent without leave, a chapter that preceded his eventual rise in professional wrestling.As Orton’s WWE career continued, his look became more and more synonymous with his nickname, The Viper, and the character’s tattoos contributed to an intimidating presentation, making for a cohesive look that separated him from other wrestlers. Although wrestling personas are carefully developed for television, his body art also contains personal references that extend beyond the character.How Randy Orton’s tattoos reflect family and faithSeveral of Orton’s tattoos have meanings connected to his family and beliefs. One of the most notable is the Bible verse 1 Peter 5:8. This references vigilance and the presence of an adversary. Located on his arm it makes it a visible part of his tattoo collection and adds a religious component to the designs associated with his wrestling persona.His family tributes offer a more intimate side of the artwork. Orton has his daughter Alanna’s name and birthdate represented on his arm, with Roman numerals used for the date. A red and green rose tattoo on his left bicep has also been described as a tribute to his daughter, bringing floral imagery into a collection otherwise known for darker and more aggressive designs.Other tattoos reflect his relationship with his wife, Kimberly Kessler, whom he married in 2015. The name “Kim” and a heart on his left ring finger serve as a personal tribute to their marriage. Orton also has small lettering on his left rib cage that matches a tattoo on Kessler’s collarbone, providing another connection between their body art.These designs contrast with the skulls and tribal patterns associated with The Viper, while the larger pieces contribute to his on-screen image, the family-related tattoos carry meanings tied to relationships outside WWE. Together, they show how his collection combines professional identity with personal milestones rather than serving only as a visual statement.How Randy Orton’s tattoos shaped The Viper’s lookOrton’s transformation into The Viper involved more than his wrestling style and signature moves, and his increasingly extensive tattoos became a defining part of his appearance, reinforcing the character’s dangerous, unpredictable presentation. The interlocking tribal patterns and skull imagery across his arms helped create a recognisable silhouette that remained consistent throughout different stages of his WWE career.His upper-back tribal tattoo dates to his developmental wrestling period in Ohio Valley Wrestling. Reports about the design describe complications with its healing during training, which reportedly required further work. As Orton gained experience and became a main-event performer, additional tattoos expanded the visual identity established by that early piece. The religious and floral elements add contrast, preventing the collection from being defined solely by aggressive imagery.Orton’s tattoos have therefore become part of his wider presentation as a WWE veteran. They distinguish him in promotional photography, television appearances and video-game character models, where wrestlers’ visual details are recreated for audiences. Their visibility has also made the artwork relevant to conversations about how athletes and entertainers are represented in commercial media.Why Randy Orton’s tattoos sparked a copyright lawsuitOrton’s tattoos attracted legal attention through a dispute involving tattoo artist Catherine Alexander, who created several of the designs on his body between 2003 and 2008. Alexander argued that reproducing the tattoos on Orton’s likeness in WWE video games infringed her copyrights. The case involved WWE, Take-Two Interactive and other companies connected to the games.The dispute raised a question that extends beyond wrestling: who controls the reproduction rights to artwork inked on another person’s body? Although Orton wears the tattoos, Alexander argued that she retained copyright in the original designs. The issue became particularly relevant as video games increasingly sought to reproduce athletes and entertainers with realistic detail. It also revealed that copyright questions can arise when artwork permanently attached to a person’s body is reproduced commercially.The case did not mean that any tattoo appearing in a video game was automatically an infringement. The legal outcome was determined by the particular facts of the dispute and the rights at stake. But it did bring more attention to the need for entertainment companies to think about tattoo designs when building realistic character models, promo material and other commercial representations.The lawsuit added an unexpected twist to the tale of Orton’s body art. His tattoos had been a long-standing part of his personal identity and wrestling persona, but the dispute showed they could also become a matter of intellectual property law. The case clarified the difference between a performer’s likeness and the separately created artwork that appears on that likeness.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice for Week 8
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone shares his lineup advice for every position.
articles.body:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 8 rankings .

Prescott is coming off a three-touchdown game that helped him finish as the QB6 overall last week. It was his first multiple-TD outing since Week 2.

Now, he faces one of his easiest matchups of the season against a Cardinals defense allowing the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks, including at least two touchdowns to the last six QBs they've faced. The Cowboys also have the highest implied team total on the week at 30.75, so you can expect another top-half QB1 finish from Prescott.

Jacoby Brissett at Cowboys – On the other side of that game, the Cowboys are giving up the eighth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Brissett is always risky, but his last matchup with an easy opponent resulted in a top-10 fantasy finish. I'm expecting something similar this time around.

Kyler Murray at Lions – Murray is still getting comfortable in Kevin O'Connell's offense and a date with the Lions should help. Detroit is the most generous defense to fantasy QBs, with multiple TDs allowed to every quarterback its encountered, including at least three touchdowns to four of those six passers. Murray has also been more productive with his legs lately, which boosts his fantasy floor and ceiling.

Fantasy managers might not realize just how valuable White can be at the moment as a solid RB2 with Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR. Prior to the Commanders' Week 7 bye, White handled nearly 70% of the snaps, coming away with 57 yards and a score. That's the third time in his last four outings where White has posted either 80-plus yards or a touchdown. While Washington is well rested after a week off, the Eagles — who are already banged up — will be playing on a short week after appearing on Monday Night Football. Philly's once-feared defense has lost its teeth, allowing some huge stat lines over the last month.

With Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols only playing supporting roles, White is positioned to be a top-24 fantasy back in Week 8 and possibly longer.

Bhayshul Tuten vs. Colts – Tuten has been remarkably consistent with his yardage totals this season, with at least 87 scrimmage yards in five of his six appearances. Coming off the bye week, Tuten and the Jags are 10-point favorites against a Colts team that just traded away defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and guard Quenton Nelson. Consider Tuten a borderline low-end RB1 this week.

Jordan Mason at Lions – Aaron Jones Sr. returned to practice on Thursday, but it's clear he's not 100% after battling through a knee injury recently. Mason handled 15 carries for 68 yards last week and should see the bulk of the touches yet again. In his only two appearances this year, Mason has racked up 127 yards and a touchdown on 30 carries.

Blake Corum vs. Chargers – Corum has found the end zone in three straight games, while putting up at least 60 scrimmage yards in each of those contests. The Rams are 9-point favorites over a Chargers team that's permitting the ninth-most fantasy points to running backs. This is another spot where Corum can deliver top-24 RB production behind Kyren Williams.

It might seem insane to have Wilson listed as a Start after his disappointing performances the last three weeks since Marvin Harrison Jr. was removed from the picture. Wilson has been the WR52, WR56 and WR24 in weekly scoring, with stat lines of 4-30-0, 4-32-0 and 4-55-0 (with 11 rushing yards). He's also been held to eight targets or less in each of those games, after earning 30 targets the prior two weeks before Harrison's departure.

Now, Wilson gets a shootout with a Cowboys defense that's allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to his position. That makes him a viable fantasy WR2 this week. However, if you have Wilson, you should strongly consider moving him after this performance since he'll face the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs the following three weeks.

DJ Moore vs. Ravens – We've barely seen the DJ Moore experience this season, since he's only taken the field for 60% of the snaps in two contests due to injuries. In those two outings, Moore combined for 18 targets, 11 catches, 167 yards and a touchdown. The upside remains high when healthy, especially in a game tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 54.5.

Garrett Wilson vs. Raiders – Fantasy managers are down on Wilson after back-to-back quieter games, but let's not forget he was the WR12 after the first five weeks. Wilson voiced his displeasure with the recent reduced targets on the sideline during last week's loss to the Dolphins and it's setting up a squeaky-wheel situation. The Raiders have allowed double-digit fantasy points to six different receivers over the last month, and I'd expect Wilson to join that list.

Stefon Diggs vs. Eagles – With Terry McLaurin out for the year, the Commanders' receiving corps is going to look a little different coming out of the bye. While Diggs' role might not change that much, he's likely to see more targets. That's notable against an Eagles defense that's giving up the second-most fantasy points to receivers, the sixth-most receiving yards and the ninth-most receiving touchdowns. In the last four games, six WRs have posted at least 70 yards against Philly.

Henry has been a streaky fantasy player in the past, so I tend to not get too excited when he puts together three or four strong performances. We're currently in the midst of that kind of stretch with stat lines of 5-62-0, 3-44-1, 4-48-1 and 7-71-0 over the last month. Fortunately, this week he gets a Dolphins defense that's giving up the third-most fantasy points to tight ends. In its last five outings, Miami has allowed at least one touchdown to five different tight ends and the only game during that stretch where it didn't let a TE find the end zone, T.J. Hockenson hit them up for 13 catches and 119 yards.

Henry is a solid fantasy TE1 once again and even someone you could consider as a flex option this week, especially with A.J. Brown's health concerns.

T.J. Hockenson at Lions – Speaking of Hockenson, he's also a quality start this week against a Lions defense permitting the most fantasy points to tight ends. That includes 10 touchdowns given up to the position in six games.

Brenton Strange vs. Colts – As I mentioned in this week's waiver wire article, Strange is averaging the sixth-most targets among tight ends over the last month and has posted three very usable stat lines of 7-95-0, 7-68-0 and 5-44-0. That includes two top-12 weekly fantasy finishes. Follow that volume into a game versus a spiraling Colts squad.

Mahomes is the featured quarterback to sit for the second straight week after the Seahawks caused him to finish in the single digits for fantasy points. After starting the season with two straight top-10 fantasy results, Mahomes hasn't cracked the QB1 range in his last four games (QB20, QB13, Q23, QB25).

Injuries to his pass-catchers and offensive line have been part of the problem and are only amplified more in tougher matchups. The Broncos fit that description, especially with Pat Surtain II trending towards a return from his ankle injury.

It's also worth noting, Mahomes isn't running as much coming off the ACL last season, as expected. After averaging over 30 rushing yards per contest in 2025, he's under 12 yards per game this year.

Caleb Williams at Seahawks – Williams gets the unenviable draw of facing the Seahawks' stifling defense this week. Seattle has held opposing QBs to the second-fewest passing yards and fantasy points this season.

Bo Nix vs. Chiefs – Nix finally had a good fantasy day in Week 7, but it was mostly thanks to a fluky 62-yard TD run. I wouldn't expect much from him against a Chiefs defense giving up the third-fewest fantasy points to QBs, including Nix himself, who only managed 131 passing yards, one TD, one interception and two rushing yards in their Week 1 matchup.

Hampton only topped six fantasy points once in the four games before the Chargers' Week 7 bye. We also watched as this backfield became a true three-man, hot-hand committee, with Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell.

It's possible Mike McDaniel and the coaching staff made adjustments during their time off and are ready to fix the long list of problems with this offense, but expecting that to happen against the Rams is a stretch.

Sean McVay's crew are 7-point favorites and if the Chargers are trailing, that could limit Hampton's upside, since the routes run were split almost evenly in their last outing (Hampton 15, Vidal 13, Mitchell 12). I'm treating Hampton as a TD-or-bust RB3 until further notice.

Quinshon Judkins at Steelers – Judkins returned from injury with his best stat line of the season, compiling 104 yards and two touchdowns against the Titans. Those were impressive totals considering he only played 53% of the snaps, while Dylan Sampson handled 46%. Sampson also ran more routes (15-9). It seems likely that Sampson being back will limit Judkins' pass-catching role, which pushes Judkins into more of a TD-or-bust RB3 range in a matchup on the road with a tougher Steelers defense.

Rico Dowdle vs. Browns – Dowdle's 15-touch, 86-yard performance against the Saints needs to be graded on a curve since New Orleans plays a fast-paced style and allows the most fantasy points to RBs. That caused Dowdle's usual 10 touches to inflate to 15. Jaylen Warren remains the clear lead back in Pittsburgh, making Dowdle too volatile to start in fantasy most weeks.

J.K. Dobbins vs. Chiefs – In Jonah Coleman's first game off IR, the rookie turned the Broncos backfield into a three-man committee and led the way by playing almost 50% of the snaps. That left Dobbins and RJ Harvey to share the other 50%. Coleman has provided the most juice in his limited action, while Dobbins hasn't been very efficient with his touches. In a difficult matchup with the Chiefs, Dobbins is far too risky to trust in your lineup given the recent trends in Denver's RB usage.

Though Odunze is a quality real-life receiver, his role in the Bears' passing attack isn't leading to major fantasy production. After slow starts, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland have gotten back on track, but Odunze has yet to find the end zone and has only topped 55 yards on two occasions.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks defense is giving up the fewest fantasy points to receivers and has only let two wideouts top 60 yards against them this season.

It's always possible Odunze could make a big play and finish with a fine stat line; this just isn't the matchup I want to take a chance on.

Jaylen Waddle vs. Chiefs – Waddle has been one of the biggest disappointments of the fantasy season and is now dealing with a chest injury. Denver's No. 1 receiver has only gone over 50 yards once in seven games and has just a single touchdown in a Broncos' uniform. This week, he gets to deal with a Chiefs defense that's the second-worst matchup for fantasy WRs and held him to one catch for two yards in the opener.

Xavier Worthy at Broncos – Worthy's big-play ability is always enticing, but as we saw last week, he fades in difficult matchups. The third-year wideout has never posted more than 25 yards against the Broncos and, to make matters worse, Patrick Surtain II is likely returning to the lineup.

Josh Downs at Jaguars – Downs hasn't gone over 50 yards in any of his last four games and is still searching for his first touchdown of 2026. His only hope for future fantasy value would be a trade to a contender.

With injuries at the position and four teams on bye — including starting tight ends like George Kittle and Isaiah Likely — it's difficult to recommend sitting any tight end in the top 20.

Freiermuth earns the mention as a potential sit, since he has yet to reach 50 yards in any game this season. He's also been held to 20 yards or less in three of his last four contests. Freiermuth is always a threat to score a touchdown and he did just that against the Browns back in Week 4. But if you're starting him this week, just know that without a TD, he's likely to let you down.

Tyler Higbee vs. Chargers – After eclipsing 60 yards in three consecutive games, Higbee has fallen back to earth with stat lines of 4-22-0 and 2-14-0. The Chargers are the ninth-toughest matchup for fantasy tight ends, but that likely won't matter. The Rams will get up in this game and lean on the run.

Mike Gesicki vs. Titans – Gesicki has scored five TDs this season, which has masked some very weak box scores otherwise. In the past two games, Gesicki's only catch in each outing was for a short touchdown. He managed just three targets during that span. That's the most TD-or-bust profile I've ever seen.

articles.title: WWE's Triple H Reacts to Christian Watson Return Video, Jokes Packers WR Needs Entrance Music
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer and head of creative Triple H acknowledged Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson's dramatic return to Lambeau Field in an ambulance during Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
WWE Hall of Famer and head of creative Triple H acknowledged Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson's dramatic return to Lambeau Field in an ambulance during Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers.

During a postgame interview, Watson noted that he used to watch WWE when he was younger, and while making his return on Thursday, he said he felt like he was watching "SmackDown vs. Raw."

Triple H gave Watson props for his toughness, while also quipping that he needed to get "some entrance music."

While making a 53-yard catch during the second quarter, Watson hit the ground hard, and he had to come out of the game with what was being called a chest injury at the time.

Watson was transported by ambulance to a local hospital in order to undergo an X-ray and CT scan.

According to ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Watson was coughing up blood at one point and was found to have a broken rib, but when he was cleared of any other issues, he wanted to return to the game.

Cameras captured Watson's return and walk down the tunnel, and once he made it back to the sidelines, he was the recipient of cheers from the crowd and support from his teammates.

Remarkably, Watson returned to the game a short time later and made two more catches during the second half, finishing the game with eight grabs for 113 yards.

Many times over the years, a WWE wrestler has been stretchered off or taken away in an ambulance during a match only to return, and Watson pulled it off during an NFL game on Thursday.

articles.title: Arsenal boss Arteta fires ‘Disneyland’ warning at Dowman after red card
articles.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says he blasted Max Dowman for red card in shock cup loss at Fleetwood.
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta warned Max Dowman he was “not in Disneyland” after the teenage rising star was sent off in the Gunners’ shock League Cup defeat by lowly Fleetwood.

The Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing losses in their history when, after the fourth-round tie ended 1-1 in normal time, they lost 5-3 on penalties away to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday.

To make matters worse for the Gunners, Dowman saw red five minutes before the end of normal time.

Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off.

Arteta’s reaction on the touchline was criticised by some pundits, who felt he should have been more sympathetic towards Dowman, who is now starting an immediate three-game ban for violent conduct after Arsenal lost an appeal against his red card and punishment.

But an unrepentant Arteta defended his response to Dowman’s red card in a pre-match news conference on Friday ahead of Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool.

“I understand. But you need to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out [for the match].

“You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with 10, you want to see that? What do you expect? I don’t know … This is the environment, and this is the reality.

“Otherwise, we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League.”

Dowman has been carefully nurtured by Arsenal since making his debut when he was just 15.

“We look after him so much, but at the same time we’re going to be demanding because he needs to earn the right to play, just like everybody else,” said Arteta, whose side are level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City

“It is not the first time. It happened another time this month with England [Under-19s]. And it will continue to happen because of the way he plays and the way he attracts opponents, and that’s it.

“We have to be able to tell each other what we think because he is 16 and we have to be very protective of him, but at the same time very straight with him about what we expect of him towards the team, individuals and the club.”

Arteta, himself a former Arsenal midfielder, insisted he had “no issues” with Dowman as the Spanish boss lamented the failure of the Gunners’ appeal.

“I’m very disappointed, to be fair, especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action,” he said.

articles.title: Which NHL wage tracker has a Winnipeg Jets fan launched after Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin received an unpaid suspension
articles.summary: A Winnipeg Jets fan has created a wage tracker website to monitor Dylan Larkin's financial losses during his unpaid suspension from the Detroit Red Wings, highlighting the implications of player-team conflicts in the NHL.
articles.body: Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin is the focus of a new NHL wage-tracking website following his suspension without pay. The project, called LarkinLosses.com, was launched by the anonymous creator behind Hellebucks.com, a site that previously tracked the money Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck forfeited during his suspension.The creator describes himself as a Winnipeg Jets fan with a knack for numbers. The new tracker puts a financial figure on Larkin’s ongoing absence as uncertainty grows around his future in Detroit.How Dylan Larkin’s Detroit Red Wings suspension inspired LarkinLosses.comLarkinLosses.com was launched by the anonymous individual who previously created Hellebucks.com. The creator has described himself as a Winnipeg Jets fan with a particular interest in numbers, bringing the same salary-tracking concept to another high-profile NHL situation.The earlier website attracted attention during Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension from the Winnipeg Jets. Rather than simply reporting the goaltender’s absence, Hellebucks.com displayed the money he was losing as the suspension continued. Its real-time approach gave fans an easy way to follow the financial consequences of the dispute.The new project applies that idea to Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings. It also demonstrates how online fan projects can turn complicated contract details and disciplinary decisions into information that is easy for hockey followers to understand.How much money is Dylan Larkin losing daily?If the numbers in the report are correct, Dylan Larkin is losing well over $41,000 for each day that he sits out with no pay. That’s a figure that makes the length of his absence that much more significant, with the total losses mounting with each passing day.If this goes on for a few weeks, the financial implications could be significant, and a long-term suspension could push the number into six figures and beyond, depending on how long Larkin is out of the Detroit Red Wings’ lineup.Larkin was suspended after reportedly telling the organization he would not play for them, a major shift in the relationship between the forward and the franchise he has played for throughout his NHL career.Larkin has been a stalwart for the Detroit Red Wings through some rough seasons. He was a big part of the rebuilding process and the team’s attempts to get back into contention as a leader and captain, so there’s more to this current spat than just the immediate financial effects.What happened during Connor Hellebuyck’s suspension?The creator's previous project offers a useful comparison for understanding the potential scale of Larkin's losses. Hellebucks.com reportedly tracked $927,835 in forfeited wages over Connor Hellebuyck's 24-day suspension from the Winnipeg Jets.Hellebuyck's saga ended with him being traded to the New Jersey Devils on Oct. 23, 2026, according to reports. The website's counter had tracked the financial toll during the lockout and had made the dispute a closely followed online story for NHL fans.What LarkinLosses.com offers supporters is a similar way to keep tabs on the Detroit Red Wings captain's situation, but the two aren't the same, and how much Larkin eventually loses will depend on how quickly the dispute is settled.Why is the website important to the Detroit Red Wings?The creation of LarkinLosses.com proves the NHL’s fascination with player-team disputes. The site is a fan-made independent project, not an official league tracker, but it does shine a light on the financial ramifications of suspensions without pay.For the Detroit Red Wings, the priority remains finding a resolution to the situation involving their captain; if trade discussions are underway, the organization will need to assess possible destinations and the value of any return before making a major decision.For now, Larkin's daily wage losses provide a visible measure of how long the uncertainty continues. The website's counter is likely to remain a talking point among fans until the forward's future with the Detroit Red Wings becomes clearer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranking the 10 Most Absurd Athlete Halloween Costumes
articles.summary: The Halloween spirit is already in full swing in the sports world.
articles.body:
The Halloween spirit is already in full swing in the sports world.

Every year, professional athletes across all major leagues get creative and wow us with elaborate costumes that give us a peek into their off-court interests. It's always a blast to see how far Halloween-enthusiast athletes can go with a big platform and a bigger payday to bring their costumes to life.

Who could forget LeBron James as Edward Scissorhands in 2019?

That happened to be the same year Dwight Howard fully committed to the bit in a full Thanos get-up:

As 2026 Halloweekend rolls in, let's take a look at the 10 most absurd athlete Halloween costumes that players have entertained us with so far this season.

No. 10: 49ers WR Ricky Pearsall as Austin Powers

Foxxy Cleopatra obviously steals the show here, but the beauty of a couples costume is the ability to aura farm.

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall made a groovy Austin Powers alongside Foxxy and let her shine, just like the real Austin Powers would.

No. 9: Penguins Forward Rickard Rakell as Jack Skellington

If Victor Wembanyama isn't going to do it, somebody has to.

We're glad Pittsburgh Penguins forward Rickard Rakell and his partner took on the responsibility of the Jack Skellington and Nightmare Before Christmas costume this year, because they killed it.

The full dedication with the body and face paint. The wig. The accurate outfits and personal touches. This is a well-done Halloween costume, and it reminded us that you don't always have to do the absolute most to make an impact.

No. 8: Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs as Michael Jackson

There's something great about the fact that Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs chose to rock Michael Jackson's Super Bowl XXVII performance outfit.

This isn't your run-of-the-mill Thriller fan, this is a ball-knower. Let's hope he moonwalks into the end zone on Sunday.

No. 7: Bruins Goalie Jeremy Swayman as Costco Employee

Who doesn't love a free sample or 20 on a Costco run?

We only hope the Swaymans were handing out actual pizza rolls.

No. 6: Mammoth Defenseman Andrew Peeke as Justin and Britney

No. 5: Capitals Forward Tom Wilson as Castaway

Sometimes the beauty of a costume is the personal touch, and that couldn't be more accurate for Capitals forward Tom Wilson and former pro volleyball player wife Taylor. They used Halloween to announce that their family is expecting , with the help of a 2000s Tom Hanks classic.

Taylor Wilson captioned the photo referencing the famous quote from Castaway : "Baby WILSONNNNN! #2 coming March 2027"

No. 4: Lions QB Jared Goff as Bobby Boucher

Putting on the costume is only half the battle. The other half is committing to the bit.

Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff fully committed to his Bobby "The Waterboy Boucher" bit this Halloween.

The absurdity of the costume is even better when you consider the awesome season Goff is having compared to the character he's portraying. He's the first quarterback in NFL history to throw at least 14 touchdowns without turning the ball over once through the first six games of a season.

No. 3: Bruins Defenseman Nikita Zadorov as The Nutcracker

File Boston Bruins defenseman Nikita Zadorov's costume as "unintentionally terrifying."

Zadorov and his family are known for their yearly halloween photo shoots. This one definitely didn't disappoint.

The whole squad teamed up for a Nutcracker look, with Zadorov completely decked out as the Nutcracker himself. It's an accomplishment that none of the kids are screaming or crying at this terrifying sight.

No. 2: Knicks C Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods as 'Game of Thrones' Characters

Knicks superstar Karl-Anthony Towns and wife Jordyn Woods win "most elaborate costume of the year" so far with their ultra-realistic Game Of Thrones -inspired couples costume.

Towns dressed as the Night King, complete with facial prosthetics, body paint, armor and a "weapon." Woods was a White Walker, with all of the special effects and makeup to elevate the concept.

Best of all, HBO Max and the Knicks gave us a behind-the-scenes look into just how much effort costumes like this take.

Everyone say thank you to Towns for making sure we were treated to a championship-caliber costume this year.

No. 1: 49ers CB Nate Hobbs as Daejon Love

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy hosted a bye-week Halloween party, and some solid costumes came out of it. None came close to actual 49ers cornerback Nate Hobbs dressing up as the infamous Daejon Love .

Love was arrested and indicted on federal wire fraud charges earlier this year for posing as a 49ers player on dating sites and social media and scamming people for money.

Sometimes, the best costumes aren't about the elaborate makeup. They're a result of thinking, "I have the opportunity to do the funniest thing right now," and actually doing it.

articles.title: Chelsea vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: Manchester United appeared set to sack Michael Carrick this week, but he may have one chance to save his job – at Chelsea.
articles.body:
Who: Chelsea vs Manchester United What: English Premier League Where: Stamford Bridge in London, United Kingdom When: Saturday, October 31 at 12:30pm (12:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 9:30 GMT

With Manchester United fans on standby for news of Michael Carrick’s sacking this week, an unexpected show of patience has given the under-fire boss a new lease of life.

When Carrick was pictured driving into United’s Carrington training base on Monday – just 24 hours after a miserable 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth – it was widely expected he would be dismissed within hours.

Instead, United’s hierarchy sprang a major surprise by keeping Carrick, for now at least.

Whether Carrick can avoid becoming the third manager to be sacked by United powerbroker Ratcliffe since he purchased a minority stake in the club in 2024 remains in doubt .

United have been in miserable form and sit just one point above the relegation zone ahead of Saturday’s trip to fifth-placed Chelsea.

Without a victory in eight games in all competitions – and off to their worst league start in 40 years – United must beat Chelsea to help Carrick stave off the axe.

But with captain Bruno Fernandes dropped last weekend after criticising Carrick’s tactics and defender Lisandro Martinez fined for blasting the club’s transfer policy, Carrick’s side are far from united.

What is the latest on the Fernandes fallout with Carrick?

What Carrick called a “pure football” decision to drop Fernandes backfired as ⁠⁠⁠⁠United imploded and tumbled to 16th, with the forlorn Portuguese watching from the bench – a defeat that piled more pressure on Carrick, even as fans cheered the manager while booing the squad.

Fernandes was benched after criticising United’s tactics following the 4-1 Champions League thrashing by Como, leaving Carrick facing a ⁠⁠⁠⁠dilemma ahead of the Chelsea clash.

Should he continue to sideline his captain or recall his most creative player after United badly missed his influence against Bournemouth? The loss left United with seven points from eight matches.

Despite winning England’s Player of the Year honours last season, Fernandes has struggled for form in this campaign, yet United appeared even more toothless without their playmaker orchestrating play from midfield on Sunday.

“It was a decision based on what we felt was right for the game. That’s it,” Carrick told a news conference on Thursday.

“Bruno is fully committed to this football club and there are absolutely no issues. We move forward, make decisions as we go and focus on Saturday’s game.”

He said Fernandes remains captain after clear-the-air talks.

“My responsibility is to the players … Of course we’ve spoken. We have meetings. The boys are hungry. We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better,” Carrick added.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has insisted teenage rising star Estevao will feature for the club this season after the Brazil midfielder spent Wednesday’s League Cup loss to Liverpool at Anfield on the bench.

Blues fans spent much of the 1-1 draw, which led to a 6-5 loss on penalties, chanting the 19-year-old Estevao’s name as he warmed up in front of them.

But despite the match being deadlocked at 1-1 from late in the first half, former Liverpool star Alonso resisted the temptation to bring on Estevao, who has played only 47 minutes in the Premier League this season, with his two starts coming in the League Cup.

“We started with Pedro (Neto), with Danny (Welbeck) and with Morgan (Rogers) up front,” said Alonso.

“The game had very intense moments. We knew that it was going to be physical.

“And after we had to deal with Moi (Caicedo), he had little problems. Malo (Gusto), as well, he had cramps. So we were a little bit forced with substitutions.”

Estevao’s lack of action in the match was in stark contrast to when he grabbed the headlines in scoring the winner against Liverpool in their Premier League clash last October.

“I understand (Estevao’s) situation and he could be happier for sure. He wants to play and to be part of the team,” said Alonso of a player who cost a reported 29 million pounds ($39m) when Chelsea signed him from Palmeiras in 2024, though, he only joined them a year later.

“There will be moments for everything. I’m sure Este will have his moments – that’s my responsibility.

“We know that the season is going to be long and there will be moments for everyone. Trust me, Este is going to play his role.”

Alonso backs Estevao for bigger role at Chelsea

Alonso dismissed ⁠⁠⁠⁠media speculation on Friday about ⁠⁠⁠⁠a January loan move for the forward.

The ⁠⁠⁠⁠19-year-old’s lack of playing time has seen Alonso scrutinised, especially given the Blues’ League Cup exit followed the 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham Hotspur last week.

Asked at a news conference if Estevao could go out on loan, Alonso said: “No discussions about that.

“The season is long and there will be moments for everyone. It’s a process for the team, for Este, for myself.

“But I’m sure that ‌‌‌‌in the season he’ll have his games, his minutes. And we’re still early in the season but he’ll be there.

“It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch; they want to be playing.

“And when any of them haven’t had enough minutes because ⁠⁠⁠⁠of my decision, I have to take the responsibility ⁠⁠⁠⁠for that, that they are not as happy as they could be.”

What happened the last time Chelsea played Man United?

Manchester United were 1-0 winners at Chelsea in the Premier League when the sides last met.

Matheus Cunha scored the only goal just before half-time in April’s clash.

Chelsea lost home and away to United last season, but did win the previous season’s battle at Stamford Bridge.

Marc Cucurella’s 77th-minute strike was the only goal of the game in May 2025.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Chelsea a 53 percent chance of winning the game, while only offering United a 23.5 percent chance of claiming all three points.

This will be the 200th meeting between the clubs in a fixture that dates back to December 1905 – a goalless draw in Manchester in the old Division Two (now the Championship).

United have won 82 of the encounters, while Chelsea have emerged victorious on 56 occasions and there have been 61 draws.

Chelsea carry a lengthy injury list with forward Joao Pedro and captain Reece James ⁠⁠⁠⁠sidelined, while defender Maxence Lacroix is also expected to miss a few weeks with a hamstring injury suffered in Wednesday’s ⁠⁠⁠⁠loss at Anfield.

“Max picked up an injury and we ⁠⁠⁠⁠expect he is not going to be ready before the (November 9-17) international break,” Alonso said. “He will be a few weeks out.”

There was better news on midfielder Moises Caicedo, who is available despite being forced off ‌‌‌‌against Liverpool with a minor issue. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez also misses out, but could return before the international break as he recovers from a jaw injury.

“We still need to wait ‌‌‌‌until ‌‌‌‌next week, but there’s a chance. In case he (Martinez) is ready to play, he will probably need a face mask,” Alonso said.

Penders; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Gusto; Henderson, Lavia, Caicedo; Neto, Palmer, Rogers

Kobbie Mainoo has resumed training after a knock, but the match is likely to come too soon for Marcus Rashford’s return.

Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Manuel Ugarte and Patrick Dorgu are all still confirmed to be missing out.

articles.title: Lakers List Key Starter on Injury Report for Warriors Game
articles.summary: Ziaire Williams is questionable for the NBA Cup opener in San Francisco, but Luka Doncic is off the report.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers head to San Francisco on Friday night to face the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center, and they will do it with one of their starters listed as questionable.

Small forward Ziaire Williams is questionable with left foot and heel injury management, while point guard Luka Doncic is off the injury report after sitting out Wednesday's game with back tightness.

Williams missed Wednesday's game against the Clippers with left foot soreness, as the Lakers were on the second night of a back-to-back and ruled out both him and Doncic before tipoff.

Head coach JJ Redick explained the thinking before that game, telling reporters, as reported by the Los Angeles Times' Broderick Turner , that both players woke up sore and tight.

"We have a tough stretch of games. Not a lot of time between [games so] just being overly cautious," Redick said.

Redick was also asked if both players would be ready for Friday and said that was the hope, which has already come true for Doncic.

Williams is still a game-time call after missing the Clippers rematch , and Friday's matchup is the Lakers' fourth game in six days, so I understand the caution.

Williams has started all four games he has played this season, averaging 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.3 assists while shooting 57.1% from the field and 46.7% from three.

He has given the Lakers good scoring for a player whose main job is defense, so losing him would take one of the Lakers' better wing defenders off the floor against a Warriors team that takes plenty of threes.

Center Walker Kessler is also on the Lakers' injury report but is available and will keep wearing a splint on his left finger.

Kessler has played in all five games and is averaging 14.8 points and 8.2 rebounds.

Rookie shooting guard Cameron Carr is out with a right oblique strain and has yet to make his NBA debut, and small forward Adou Thiero is out with left knee injury management.

The Lakers have also already won without key pieces, since they beat the Clippers 103-87 on Wednesday without Doncic and Williams, as shooting guard Quentin Grimes scored 23 points and led a strong defensive night , while shooting guard Collin Sexton gave them a big lift off the bench .

Doncic being back is the biggest news for this game, since he is averaging 36.0 points per game, and he scored 28 points when the Lakers beat the Warriors 127-105 on opening night.

The Lakers are 4-1, and this game is also their NBA Cup opener, so a win would give them a strong start in group play.

Golden State is 2-3 but has won two straight, and the Warriors will be without small forward Jimmy Butler, shooting guard Moses Moody and center Kristaps Porzingis.

If Williams can play, I like the Lakers to win this one, because I think their starting group with Doncic and Williams together is one of the best in the West.

After Friday, the Lakers return home to face the Toronto Raptors on Sunday and the Miami Heat on Monday.

articles.title: Brett Yormark’s immediate reaction to leaving Big 12 conference in 2027
articles.summary: As the Big 12 conference has had Brett Yormark as its commissioner since 2022, he has been a part of major events happening like the conference realignment t...
articles.body:
As the Big 12 conference has had Brett Yormark as its commissioner since 2022, he has been a part of major events happening like the conference realignment that had big programs join in 2023 and 2024. Fast forward to the present, and the Big 12 conference will go through more major change, this time in the search for a new commissioner as Yormark is leaving the role.

According to Brett McMurphy of On3 Sports, Yormark's statement would consist of being excited to 'pass the baton' to the future commissioner. Even after he's done being the Big 12 conference commissioner, he expresses that he will be "continuing to cheer" for success as he has been a "lifelong fan of the Big 12."

"I am looking forward to passing the baton to the next commissioner & continuing to cheer this league on as a lifelong fan of the Big 12," Yormark said in his statement.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Brett Yormark's impact on the Big 12 conference

According to ESPN, Yormark will stay in the role through January 2027 in order to ensure a smooth transition as he "prepares to take another job outside of college sports," which is not known at this moment.

In 2023, Yormark was the commissioner of the Big 12 when BYU, Cincinnati, Houston, and UCF joined the conference, as the job wasn't done, with 2024 having Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado, and Utah join when the Pac-12 was going through a breakup. Yormark continued in his statement by saying that whoever the next commissioner of the Big 12 is, they "will inherit a conference that is 16 strong."

"When I accepted this job, my goal was to put this conference on an upward trajectory and truly believe that the future of the conference could not be in better shape," Yormark said. "The next commissioner of this league will inherit a conference that is 16 strong. There has never been a better time to be a member of the Big 12 than right now."

At any rate, it remains to be seen who will replace Yormark and what his next venture will be, as it won't involve college sports.
