articles.title: After Heartbreaking Internet Invitational Moment, Peter Finch Sends Team a Personal Message
articles.summary: Episode 2 of the Internet Invitation is in the books, and it includes one of the most incredible finishes in YouTube golf history. After a crushing defeat on...
articles.body:
Episode 2 of the Internet Invitation is in the books, and it includes one of the most incredible finishes in YouTube golf history. After a crushing defeat on a 20-foot clutch putt in the second of two playoff holes, Team Blue, led by Peter Finch, was eliminated.

It was one of the most dramatic endings to an already wild episode, and for Team Blue, it was the end of the road, with all 16 members of the team no longer able to win their share of $4 million.

Finch Sends Personal Message To His Team

After the loss, captain Finch posted a video thanking his team for everything they brought to the table. "Guys, that was… that was a brutal way to lose. But, also, at the same time, what an amazing thing to be a part of." He added, "Just imagine, if we'd have done that, they would have been feeling on absolute cloud nine now. As it is, obviously everyone is going to be a little down in the dumps. As long as we can all leave the course saying we gave it everything that we had, that's the main thing."

"Couldn't have asked anything more of you. Thank you for having me as your captain. Hey, there's always next year."

The message was a personal thank you to his team and a way to try and lift up their spirits given the gravity of the heartbreaking loss.

Roger Steele, who played in the playoffs and was a big part of Team Blue, responded .

"Ep 2 was wild. Tried our hardest. Big John is legendary. But one thing that's going to be overlooked about first two episodes is how the whole field thought we were by far the weakest team, but we had THEE most elite captain of them all. Our belief in our pairings and strategy was at an all time high. @PeterFinchGolf sent this to us all in a group chat in the midst of the chaos. We'd play for you 8 days a week bro. Heroic stuff. Thanks Pete."

In episode one, Finch tells his team he wants the day to end in tears for someone. The reason is that Team White chose to play Team Blue, thinking they could beat them in the first round. Team Blue took that call-out personally and wanted to prove they weren't a throwaway team.

It's somewhat ironic that it was Team Blue who ended up suffering such a close defeat and is the team that needed the pick-me-up from the same captain who wanted to make their opponent cry with a loss.

This is not to call out Finch for his competitiveness. It's simply an observation that he would start the day ready to break the hearts of his opponents and it was his team that felt the ultimate loss in the end.

articles.title: One Foot in 2027, One in 2028: Nebraska’s Halloween Blackout Offers a Massive Recruiting Opportunity
articles.summary: Matt Rhule is looking to put the finishing touches on an outstanding 2027 recruiting class while laying the foundations for another talented group in 2028. W...
articles.body:
Matt Rhule is looking to put the finishing touches on an outstanding 2027 recruiting class while laying the foundations for another talented group in 2028. With Washington coming to Memorial Stadium on Halloween night, the Huskers have the perfect stage to sell their vision of the future.

There is something fitting about Nebraska hosting one of its biggest recruiting weekends of the season on Halloween. Memorial Stadium will be dressed in black, the lights will be shining, and more than 85,000 passionate Husker fans will be doing everything they can to create an intimidating atmosphere for Washington.

For Matt Rhule and his coaching staff, the occasion represents far more than another Big Ten matchup. It is an opportunity to show some of the country's most talented high school football players exactly what Nebraska football can become.

The Huskers have one foot firmly planted in 2027, with an impressive recruiting class already assembled and a handful of high-profile targets still on the board. At the same time, the coaching staff has turned its attention toward 2028, where another collection of talented prospects across multiple positions is firmly in its sights.

Nebraska has made considerable progress under Rhule, both in recruiting and on the field. However, there is one piece of the puzzle that remains frustratingly elusive: consistently beating quality Big Ten opposition.

Saturday night presents another opportunity to change that narrative.

Finishing Off a Brilliant 2027 Recruiting Class

Nebraska's 2027 recruiting class has given Husker fans plenty of reasons to be optimistic. Headlined by five-star quarterback Trae Taylor, the group features talent across the offensive and defensive lines, secondary and skill positions.

More importantly, the class has developed a sense of togetherness that could prove just as valuable as its individual talent.

Taylor has emerged as a leader of the group, with several committed players making repeated trips to Lincoln and actively encouraging other recruits to join them. That enthusiasm is particularly important when Nebraska is trying to convince highly rated prospects from across the country to make their college home in the Midwest.

The Huskers will welcome back several prominent 2027 commitments this weekend, including four-star offensive lineman Jordan Agbanoma, cornerback Jailen Hill and defensive lineman Nehemiah Ombati. Edge rusher Ma'atoe Moe, defensive lineman Jayden Travers and tight end Joey Hunter are also expected to attend.

Their presence is important for two reasons. It gives the coaching staff another opportunity to strengthen relationships with players already committed to the program, while also allowing those recruits to play a role in attracting the next generation.

But Nebraska is not finished with 2027 just yet.

One of the most intriguing remaining possibilities is five-star tight end Ahmad Hudson, who is committed to LSU but remains a player Nebraska is pursuing. The Huskers are working to get him back to campus before signing day, potentially as early as this weekend.

Nebraska is also exploring opportunities with other pass catchers and defensive prospects who could become late additions or flip candidates.

Landing another highly rated prospect would be the perfect finishing touch to a class that has already generated considerable excitement.

In today's recruiting environment, however, securing a commitment is only part of the battle. Holding on to that talent until signing day is equally important.

Programs such as Texas A&M and Florida remain interested in Agbanoma, while Moe has also attracted attention elsewhere. Getting those players back around the coaching staff, their future teammates and the Nebraska fan base is another opportunity to reinforce their decisions.

The 2028 Recruiting Machine Is Already Moving

While Nebraska looks to complete its 2027 class, the coaching staff is wasting little time establishing relationships with the next wave of prospects.

The 2028 visitor group is particularly impressive because of the variety of positions represented. Nebraska is targeting high-level talent at wide receiver, running back, tight end, offensive line, defensive line, linebacker and throughout the secondary.

Four-star receiver Ryan Richmond-McDavis is one of the most exciting offensive prospects expected in Lincoln. The St. Louis standout possesses exceptional speed, reportedly recording one of the fastest times on the Under Armour camp circuit over the summer.

For a program that has invested heavily in improving its offensive skill positions, securing an early relationship with an explosive receiver like Richmond-McDavis makes plenty of sense.

Another significant visitor is four-star tight end Izzy Johnigan, one of the nation's top prospects at his position. Johnigan has already experienced a Nebraska game day this month, having attended the Indiana matchup, and is returning for another look.

That repeat visit suggests genuine interest, but Nebraska must demonstrate that the progress being made on the field can translate into victories.

On the defensive side, four-star safety CJ Craig-James is a particularly interesting name. Nebraska entered his recruitment relatively late but has managed to secure a visit despite strong competition from SEC programs, including Auburn.

The Huskers' defensive performances should give the coaching staff plenty to discuss with Craig-James.

Nebraska enters the weekend leading the nation in third-down defense, with opponents converting just 19.3% of their opportunities. The Blackshirts also rank among the country's top 20 in total defense, scoring defense and rushing defense.

For defensive recruits, there is now tangible evidence that Nebraska can compete physically with some of the best programs in the country.

In-state linebacker Owen Price is another hugely important target. The Huskers face competition from regional rivals including Iowa, Minnesota and Kansas State, making it essential that Nebraska continues demonstrating its upward trajectory.

Meanwhile, four-star edge rusher Steven McClendon and three-star offensive lineman TJ Brandon will travel from Georgia, while California running back Noel Washington and Florida athlete Lamar Garrison add further national representation.

This is not a recruiting class being built around one position or one geographic region. Nebraska is attempting to establish a national footprint while continuing to prioritise talent closer to home.

Nebraska's 2027 Class Could Be Its Greatest Recruiting Asset

One of the most encouraging aspects of Nebraska's current recruiting operation is the willingness of committed players to help recruit others.

The 2027 class is doing more than simply showing up for photographs and enjoying a weekend in Lincoln.

Taylor and his fellow commitments have developed strong relationships, communicating regularly and encouraging one another to return to campus. When those players interact with younger recruits, they are providing something that even the most persuasive coaching staff cannot manufacture: genuine enthusiasm from future teammates.

For a 2028 prospect considering Nebraska alongside established national powers, seeing committed players repeatedly travel across the country to spend time together can make a significant impression.

It demonstrates that the players themselves believe in the direction of the program.

This is particularly important because Nebraska is attempting to build sustainable success rather than relying on one outstanding recruiting cycle.

The Huskers need to stack talented classes year after year if they want to compete with the likes of Ohio State, Indiana, Michigan and the other leading programs in the Big Ten.

The 2027 class has the potential to be an important building block. The challenge now is making sure 2028 is every bit as impressive.

There Is No Better Selling Point Than Memorial Stadium Under the Lights

Recruiting visits are about much more than facilities, presentations and conversations with coaches.

They are about giving young players a feeling of what it would be like to run onto the field wearing a Nebraska uniform.

And there are few better opportunities to create that feeling than a Halloween Blackout at Memorial Stadium.

The Huskers will wear their alternate black uniforms, the crowd will be encouraged to dress in black, and the traditional Blackshirts logo will feature prominently at midfield.

With a 7 p.m. kickoff, Nebraska can showcase the full spectacle of a prime-time Big Ten football game.

The late start also provides an important logistical advantage. High school players competing on Friday nights have more time to travel to Lincoln, allowing Nebraska to attract national prospects who might struggle to attend an early kickoff.

The atmosphere should be electric, and there is little doubt that recruits will be impressed by the passion surrounding Nebraska football.

That passion remains one of the program's greatest selling points.

Even after years of frustration, Nebraska fans continue filling Memorial Stadium, following recruiting developments and investing emotionally in the future of the program.

For a teenager deciding where to spend the next three or four years, the opportunity to play in front of that kind of support is enormously appealing.

However, the atmosphere can only do so much.

The elephant in the room is Nebraska's inability to consistently turn competitive performances against top opposition into victories.

The Huskers enter Saturday at 5-2 after consecutive three-point defeats to Indiana and Oregon. Against Oregon, Nebraska held a second-half lead before surrendering the winning score in the final minute.

Those performances demonstrate how far the program has progressed, but they also highlight the fine margins that continue to separate Nebraska from the Big Ten's leading teams.

The coaching staff can point to improved talent, a physical defense, a more balanced offense and the development taking place throughout the roster. Those are legitimate selling points.

But at some stage, Nebraska needs to stop talking about how close it is and start showing that it can consistently win these games.

Washington represents an important opportunity.

The Huskies arrive in Lincoln at 4-3 and have struggled to find consistency in Big Ten play. Nebraska will be expected to win at home, particularly after having an extra week to prepare.

For the Huskers, simply being competitive is no longer enough.

A convincing performance would send a message to the recruits watching from the sidelines that Nebraska is ready to take another step forward.

It would also provide the current 2027 commitments with further evidence that their belief in the program is justified.

There is a difference between selling potential and demonstrating progress. Saturday night offers Nebraska the opportunity to do both.

The recruiting calendar never really stops, and neither can Nebraska's efforts to close the talent gap on the Big Ten's elite.

The 2027 class represents another significant step forward in Rhule's attempt to build a roster capable of competing at the highest level. Adding one or two more blue-chip prospects would only strengthen that foundation.

But the work being done with the 2028 class could prove equally important.

With highly rated players from across the country preparing to experience Memorial Stadium, Nebraska has an opportunity to establish relationships that could shape the program for years to come.

For now, the challenge is straightforward.

Get the recruits to Lincoln. Show them the passion of the fan base. Demonstrate the culture being built within the program.

Nebraska has spent too many seasons being the team that almost gets there. The talent is improving, the defense looks the part, and the recruiting operation is gathering momentum.

A Halloween night victory in front of a packed Memorial Stadium would provide the perfect backdrop to show the next generation of Huskers that the program is ready to turn potential into results.

The 2027 class is nearly complete. The 2028 class is only beginning.

Saturday night is an opportunity to move both forward.

articles.title: Lakers at Warriors: What to watch in the Bay
articles.summary: Luka Dončić returns as the Lakers visit Golden State, with rebounding and JJ Redick’s frontcourt rotation among three things to watch.
articles.body:
The Lakers head to the Bay Area with their leading scorer returning and an opportunity to build on their strongest defensive performance of the young season.

After beating the Clippers 103-87 without Luka Dončić and Ziaire Williams, the Lakers enter their sixth game at 4-1. Golden State is coming off a 119-114 victory over Minnesota behind Stephen Curry's 44 points. The Lakers defeated the Warriors 127-105 on opening night.

Dončić's return gives Los Angeles another offensive boost, but rebounding remains a concern against a Warriors team that controlled the boards in its last outing. The Lakers also have a rotation decision after coach JJ Redick turned to Jarred Vanderbilt against the Clippers.

Dončić returns after missing the Clippers game with back tightness, bringing an NBA-leading scoring average of 36 points per game back into the lineup.

The Lakers have been among the league's most efficient offensive teams through five games. They rank second in scoring at 123.2 points per game, first in field-goal percentage at 53% and second in offensive rating at 122.5. They also rank third in 3-point percentage at 39.2%.

Dončić had 28 points, seven rebounds and eight assists in the season-opening victory over Golden State. His return gives the Lakers their primary offensive creator as they look for a second win against the Warriors.

Los Angeles will also look to carry over its defensive activity from Wednesday, when it recorded 15 steals and five blocks against the Clippers. The Lakers rank fourth in steals at 10.8 per game and lead the NBA with 24.4 points per game off turnovers, giving them another way to generate offense alongside Dončić's half-court creation.

The Lakers' offensive production has helped them win four of their first five games, but their rebounding numbers sit at the other end of the league.

L.A. ranks last in rebounds at 38 per game.

Golden State outrebounded Minnesota 53-42 in its last game, collecting 13 offensive rebounds to the Timberwolves' seven.

Those contributions throughout Golden State's lineup make rebounding a collective responsibility for the Lakers.

The Lakers' league-best shooting percentage affects how many offensive rebounding opportunities are available, so their total alone does not tell the full story. Finishing defensive possessions, however, remains an important measure of progress.

L.A. ranks 17th in defensive rating at 112.3 despite its ability to force turnovers. Limiting second chances would help the Lakers turn more initial stops into completed possessions.

Redick changed his frontcourt rotation against the Clippers, using Vanderbilt while keeping Kevon Looney on the bench.

Vanderbilt played center in smaller lineups and also appeared at power forward alongside Sandro Mamukelashvili. Whether Redick returns to those combinations is worth watching against Golden State's motion offense.

Vanderbilt gives the Lakers another option to defend on the perimeter and pursue rebounds. Playing him at center also changes how L.A. can handle switches, though those groups still must finish possessions on the boards.

Golden State also scored 54 points in the paint against Minnesota, adding another consideration as Redick determines how to divide the frontcourt minutes behind Kessler.

Williams is questionable, while Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr remain out. Williams' availability could influence how often Redick turns to Vanderbilt and which combinations he uses.

After the defensive effort against the Clippers, the Lakers will look to carry that activity into a matchup with a Warriors team coming off a win.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball Weekend Streamers: Ja'Kobe Walter, Tristan da Silva starring as injury replacements
articles.summary: Ja'Kobe Walter and Tristan da Silva lead a group of 10 players worth streaming this weekend.
articles.body:
Until Kawhi Leonard returns, Ja'Kobe Walter is a player that can be streamed with confidence. Over the last two games as a starter, Walter has averaged 18.0 points, 1.5 steals and 4.0 triples per game. The most recent timeline update for Leonard has him returning in late November, which may be the best case scenario. Walter should start until then.

There is long-term value here, but this weekend is also a favorable one for him. Toronto plays Orlando on Friday and the Lakers on Sunday, and the Raptors are currently fourth in the NBA in pace. More possessions means more stats.

Walter struggled during his rookie season but showcased real growth in year two and seems to have taken another step forward this year, despite the small sample size. His floor-spacing ability is valuable to this team with how it's currently constructed, so he should play a large reserve role, even when Leonard returns.

The 12 teams that play two games this weekend include the Celtics, Nets, Hornets, Warriors, Rockets, Pacers, Clippers, Lakers, Timberwolves, Magic, 76ers and Raptors. If you're looking to maximize your games played, prioritize picking up players from those teams.

Anthony Edwards and Jaren Jackson Jr. are among the stars that are set to miss extended periods of time.

Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is getting close to returning, so this could be the last weekend to stream Allen confidently. Allen has hit at least two three-pointers in every game this season, has scored at least 20 points twice and was even able to contribute two steals and two blocks in Charlotte's last game. 49.5 percent of the Hornets' field goal attempts this season have come from beyond the arc, which makes Allen a great fit. He'll continue to be a reliable reserve for them all year, though when Knueppel returns, his minutes and shot attempts will likely be suppressed compared to his role now.

Egor Demin (leg) is set to miss a few games, which could allow Ellis to return to the starting lineup. In three starts this season, Ellis has averaged 2.7 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.3 triples per game. He's not a high-volume scorer, though he has been able to get hot from deep in previous seasons. However, with how this roster is constructed, that won't happen often. Ellis may have some streaming appeal at times this season, but Demin and Mikel Brown Jr. will be the priority when healthy, which will prevent Ellis from being a long-term play.

Terrence Shannon Jr., G/F, Minnesota Timberwolves

With Anthony Edwards (knee) set to miss north of two months, Ayo Dosunmu has replaced him in the starting unit, which has allowed Shannon to fill in as the team's sixth man. Shannon has scored in double figures in every game this season and played a season-high 27 minutes in Minnesota's last game, the first without Edwards. Shannon has also consistently knocked down shots from beyond the arc, averaging 2.2 triples per game this year. He should be a fringe option for a couple months until Edwards returns.

He hasn't been starting even with both Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) sidelined, but da Silva continues to be productive and play big minutes. He has averaged 19.5 points and 4.5 triples per game over Orlando's last two, which lines up with when Banchero went down. He has been on fire this year, which extends back to the preseason. The short-term value over the next few weeks should be appealing, and Orlando has two games this weekend.

With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) set to miss two weeks, the Pacers will be looking for everyone to step up on offense. Nesmith had 18 points in their last game and has scored in double figures in all but one game this year, which is when he had nine points in 20 minutes in the season opener. He played 27 minutes in their last game, which was a new season high for them. They had been careful with his minutes since he's been managing his own hamstring injury, but he's back to seeing a normal workload.

Eason made his first start of the season on Wednesday with Alperen Sengun sidelined with a back injury. Sengun is questionable to play on Friday, but even if Eason doesn't start, he's been productive enough to be worth streaming in. He has averaged 1.2 steals and 1.4 blocks per game this season, and if you don't factor in the season-opener (since he was ejected after playing just three minutes), he has played 30.2 minutes per game. Could this be the Eason breakout we've been waiting for? It's worth taking a chance on him, especially with two games on the docket this weekend.

Outside of their last game, Lopez has been fantastic all season. Through the first three games of the year, Lopez averaged 18.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 2.0 triples per game. With two games scheduled this weekend, Lopez is worth taking a chance on, even if he continues to come off the bench. His production likely won't be consistent enough to be worth keeping around all year, but he's a high-upside option for short stretches.

Sandro Mamukelashvili, C, Los Angeles Lakers

It was a slow start to the year for Mamu, but he's starting to get things going. It appears head coach J.J. Redick finally realized when he has in Mamu. Over the last two games, Mamu has averaged 15 points, six rebounds, one steal, one block and 1.5 triples per game. When he gets the opportunity, Mamu has been a fantasy stud in the past. Hopefully this trend will continue for him.

Huff has been the starting center with Ivica Zubac (ankle) sidelined, and while he hasn't been great, the opportunity is too great to pass up. This is one of the riskier plays, but a starting center for two games with a history of productive fantasy lines, specifically as a shot blocker, is worth taking a chance on. As soon as Zubac is back, Huff should be dropped to the waiver wire.

Although Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff remains adamant that he wants to sign restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson , trade rumors continue to swirl around the 23-year-old.

The Swede remains away from the team, and despite the Dylan Larkin saga hogging most of the spotlight in Motown, multiple teams have shown interest in the former first-round pick.

That includes the St. Louis Blues and Seattle Kraken , as The Fourth Period's David Pagnotta reported this week.

"Talks have continued. There are (several) teams in that in that mix. I do wonder a lot about St. Louis. … I still go back to Seattle being another team. We talked about that (last week)."

Edvinsson still prefers a change of scenery over a contract, per multiple reports, and both the Blues and Kraken seem to be reasonable fits for the young blueliner.

Along with the two West clubs, Pagnotta points to the Carolina Hurricanes, San Jose Sharks and Toronto Maple Leafs as other teams with varying levels of interest.

Sportsnet hockey insider Elliotte Friedman wrote in his latest 32 Thoughts column Friday that "Boston, Nashville, St. Louis, San Jose, Seattle" are all teams with interest.

articles.title: We have lost our 7 out of 10 Newcastle United players, well all but one anyway
articles.summary: I think a lot of fans are failing to recognise the reality with these Newcastle United players. It is tunnel vision for so many Newcastle fans with Matthias...
articles.body:
I think a lot of fans are failing to recognise the reality with these Newcastle United players .

It is tunnel vision for so many Newcastle fans with Matthias Jaissle .

The media are obviously very much feeding this of course, or is that lighting the fuse?

Journalists and their bosses wanting to inflame the club's supporters, their potential customers, by wanting to make this all about Matthias Jaissle.

A sack him or back him type of thing. Constantly putting the NUFC Head Coach in the firing line is so obviously cynically done on so many occasions.

Reality is though that we have lost out 7 out of 10 Newcastle United players.

The likes of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali who were of a level where unless they had a huge off day, which happened very rarely, they were still 7 out of 10s.

Kieran Trippier the same before age caught up with them, I would also say Fabian Schar as well but he turns 35 very soon and is no longer automatic first choice.

Alexander Isak and Anthony Gordon were also 7 out of 10s but a little different than Bruno and Tonali. As in, because they were flair players and relied largely on service, they weren't 7 out of 10 every match, but over a season they were elite players who when averaged out were guaranteed to be 7 out of 10 and more!

Now we have Lewis Hall, he is our only guaranteed 7 out of 10 and is an elite player who is levels above the rest of the squad now.

Under Eddie Howe we did have other Newcastle United players who could regularly score 7 out of 10 or better at times, indeed have runs of them, BUT they had to massively work at it to do so.

As in, the likes of Murphy, Willock, Longstaff, Almiron, Joelinton and indeed Burn, they have to play at their very best to be at a similar level to those more naturally gifted players.

Reality is that now pretty much all the Newcastle United players have to be at their very best in a match to be good enough.

Sometimes they manage it, sometimes they don't.

If they all manage it together we can still potentially give anyone a game.

If though they all fail to do so we are in trouble. If some are and some aren't then could go either way in a game.

I think this is the reality of the season so far and will continue to be so.

PHOTOS: Varsity 845 cross country graduates running collegiately

Habits are hard to break, but make sure you're headed in the correct direction for Tuesday's Section 9 cross country championships.

The event, long hosted at Bear Mountain State Park, will be held at Mount Academy in Esopus.

Warwick junior Leo Shostal is the defending boys Class A champ, and he should be challenged by Monroe-Woodbury junior Leo Gowrie and Kingston seniors Redi Felton and Jackson Beesmer. Cornwall, which just won its first OCIAA meet team title, should be favored in Class B, led by senior Luke Potter and junior Colin Lewis. The girls Class A race should be challenging. Monroe-Woodbury senior Olivia Heim is the defending champ, and Kingston seniors Charlotte McFarland, Maeve Paul and Hazel Lewis have had strong seasons. Cornwall brings great top strength and would be favored in Class B, a young squad that includes top-20 OCIAA finishers Kaitlyn Hartwig, Jorie Green, Madeline Lewis. Tri-Valley senior Anna Furman is the top runner in Section 9 and should have no problem repeating as Class D champ; teammates Maria Gelsomino and Amaya Meade should bolster the Bears' team effort.

The winning team in each class race will advance to states, and the top five finishers NOT from the winning squad will also advance. The top five finishers per team will count toward point totals, while sixth- and seventh-place finishers will count toward displacing points.

The larger schools will run in the morning, followed by the smaller schools in the afternoon. articles.title: Report: Carolina’s Edvinsson Offer Sheet Wasn’t Just About Carolina
articles.summary: Elliotte Friedman says Carolina's summer offer sheet threat was never about keeping Simon Edvinsson. #RedWings
articles.body:
Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is still an unsigned restricted free agent. The Detroit Red Wings have until Dec. 1 to sign him, or to trade him to a team that will. If he is still unsigned past that date, he cannot play in the NHL this season .

Elliotte Friedman of Sportsnet added a detail this week about how close Edvinsson came to leaving in the summer. In his latest 32 Thoughts column , Friedman wrote, "I mentioned on a previous pod that Carolina, which has a history of threatening offer sheets, did so with Edvinsson. My understanding is it was right around July 1, and may have contained an added twist: they were going to trade him to a third team. Obviously, that didn't happen, and I have no information this was re-visited any time after Detroit's GM change."

The Hurricanes Were Not Planning to Keep Simon Edvinsson

The wrinkle here is not that Carolina wanted Edvinsson. Plenty of teams do. It is that the Hurricanes, by Friedman's account, were lining up a second move before the first one was even made. An offer sheet is a contract a rival club hands directly to a restricted free agent; Detroit could match it and keep him, or decline and take draft-pick compensation. Carolina never filed one, and Friedman said he has no information the idea was revisited after Detroit changed general managers. Shawn Horcoff is now running the front office on an interim basis. The third team was never identified.

It would have been a bold piece of business on a player Detroit still counts on. Edvinsson played 72 games for Detroit last season, scoring nine goals with 16 assists and a plus-12 rating. He is 23 years old. Detroit and Carolina were already linked by the offer-sheet threat itself ; the plan to flip him is new.

The Sharks and Red Wings Have Talked Extensively

Carolina is not the only team in this. The Hockey News reported Oct. 27 that St. Louis, Philadelphia, Utah, Toronto and Boston have all shown interest , with Friedman saying there is "a lot of interest in Simon Edvinsson" and that "the talks there are really picking up." Detroit, he added, has been asking those teams about young centers.

San Jose belongs on that list too. Friedman said on the 32 Thoughts podcast this week that the Sharks and Red Wings "have talked about Edvinsson pretty extensively," while adding that he is not sure what San Jose is willing to do. He did not get into what an offer would look like.

The complication is down the middle. Center Alexander Wennberg is week to week with an upper-body injury , which leaves San Jose thinner at the position right when Detroit is shopping for one. If the Red Wings want a young center such as Michael Misa, the No. 2 pick in the 2025 draft, the Sharks may not want to part with him. Macklin Celebrini is off limits in any trade. San Jose does have the prospect depth to get something done if it wants to.

Carolina Still Has Reason to Make the Offer Sheet

At this point the Hurricanes should maybe just offer sheet Edvinsson anyway and see whether Detroit matches. What do they have to lose? They are the defending Stanley Cup champions and they sit first in the Metropolitan Division at 11-2-2 . If Edvinsson does not want to be with the Red Wings anymore, Carolina would be an ideal place for him to land.

articles.title: Towns gives the Knicks another way to attack Philadelphia
articles.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns had a double-double when Philadelphia beat the Knicks on opening night. New York needs more than a repeat […]
articles.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns had a double-double when Philadelphia beat the Knicks on opening night. New York needs more than a repeat of the box score when the teams meet again Friday.

Towns finished that 106-100 loss with 19 points and 12 rebounds. Andre Drummond added 12 points and 14 boards off the bench. The production was useful, but the 76ers still controlled enough possessions to spoil New York's championship celebration.

The Knicks can make Philadelphia defend the whole floor

Towns followed with 19 points, 13 rebounds and five assists in Wednesday's comeback win at Chicago. His passing gives New York a different way to attack if the 76ers commit extra attention to Jalen Brunson. An early touch for Towns can become a scoring chance for him or a pass to a cutter before the defense is set.

I'd use those possessions alongside Brunson's pick-and-roll work rather than relying on one action all night. Philadelphia has Joel Embiid in the middle when healthy, and forcing a center to make repeated decisions away from the rim can open a different look.

Drummond gives Brown another option. His rebounding helped in the opener, and his minutes can preserve Towns without asking the starting center to handle every physical possession. The tradeoff is that the two centers create different spacing; the best choice will depend on who is defending them and which lineup is scoring.

The alternative is to lean harder on Brunson and use Towns primarily as a spot-up threat. That can work when Brunson is seeing the floor as well as he did in Chicago, where he scored 38 points with seven assists.

Friday's game starts at 7:30 p.m. Eastern in Philadelphia. Health and foul trouble can change the rotation, and the opener is only one game. The useful test is whether New York can turn its frontcourt depth into better possessions, not simply accumulate rebounds in another close loss.

The Minnesota Vikings wrapped up their practice week Friday ahead of Sunday's noon kickoff at Detroit — a week that has been quite the rollercoaster on the injury report.

Running back Aaron Jones and left guard Joe Huber both sat out Wednesday with knee injuries. Right tackle Brian O'Neill was limited with the same listed "knee" ailment. On Thursday, tight end Gavin Bartholomew was added to the list of non-participants.

Vikings at full health… except Jay Ward is suddenly questionable

Fortunately, by Friday, all four were full participants, and none of them received a game status on the final injury report . That doesn't mean the Vikings got through the week clean, though. One new name popped up on the report Friday. Jay Ward is suddenly questionable for Sunday in Detroit.

Minnesota Sports Fan (@realmnsportsfan) October 30, 2026

Ward, a fourth-year safety out of LSU, has mostly been a special teams player this season. He has played 110 special teams snaps (69%) and just four defensive snaps through six games, with six tackles. Last year, he started five games and played 248 defensive snaps.

Aaron Jones, other veterans good to go vs Lions

articles.title: Dave Canales says defensive coaching changes are about the players feeling confident
articles.summary: Panthers head coach Dave Canales fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley less than 12 hours after Thur...
articles.body:
Panthers head coach Dave Canales fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley less than 12 hours after Thursday night's loss to the Packers, and Canales said on Friday afternoon that he wants his players to be confident in their defense.

"I take that responsibility very seriously as the head coach. I know it's my responsibility to put the players in a position where they feel confident, they feel ready to go," Canales said. "I just want to see the guys connected. I want to see them excited about going out there and executing the plan, playing fast, playing physical. The effort has been there. Those things are right, but I know we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page."

Canales said he "took in a lot of information" before firing Evero and Cooley and discussed it with owner David Tepper and General Manager Dan Morgan. But he added that he made the decision himself.

"Ultimately, this is my decision. This falls squarely under the responsibilities of the head coach," Canales said. "Ultimately it had to come from me."

Todd Wash, who had been the Panthers' defensive line coach, has been promoted to defensive coordinator. Canales said Wash is great at bringing players together.

"I've known him for a long time," Canales said. "His connection with the players, he knows these guys, he knows their stories, he's connected to their lives. He pushes them hard and trains them hard, and he does a great job of earning the right to be able to push guys because of the emotional equity that he pours in. I appreciate that and I'm excited about what happens with the whole group when they get connected and play together."

articles.title: Savatgy Lands Factory Ducati Ride on Multi-Year Deal
articles.summary: Veteran joins RJ Hampshire riding the Desmo450 MX Photos by Troy Lee Designs. Troy Lee Designs Red Bull Ducati Factory Racing has signed Joey Savatgy to a mu...
articles.body:
Veteran joins RJ Hampshire riding the Desmo450 MX

Troy Lee Designs Red Bull Ducati Factory Racing has signed Joey Savatgy to a multi-year contract, adding the veteran 450 rider to Ducati's growing American off-road program alongside RJ Hampshire .

The move completes the team's two-rider lineup, with both Savatgy and Hampshire now locked into multi-year agreements across Supercross, Pro Motocross, and SuperMotocross. The duo replaces the pairing of Justin Barcia and Dylan Ferrandis who competed in the debut season for the Ducati Desmo450 MX. Having Savatgy and Hampshire signed long term allows the team to focus on development and not worrying about rebuilding the roster every offseason.

"Having Joey and RJ both committed to multi-year deals is a significant step forward for our program," said Josh Wisenor, Troy Lee Designs Race Team Manager. "The opportunity to work with both riders over multiple seasons will allow us to better understand their individual strengths, abilities, and needs, while continuing to develop the program and build on our progress heading into year two."

Savatgy also has experience racing on a relatively new motocross bike, racing for Triumph in the 2024 Pro Motocross season on the debuting TF 250-X.

The Thomasville, Georgia, native turned pro in 2013 and quickly became a 250-class threat, finishing runner-up in the 2016 250SX East Championship before stepping up to the 450 ranks in 2019. He took 450SX Rookie of the Year honors that season with the factory Kawasaki team and has since logged 13 career top-five results across the 450 ranks in Supercross, motocross, and SMX. His 2026 campaign was his strongest stretch in a while: five top-fives, 12 top-10s, a fourth at Philadelphia, and an eight-overall finish in the Supercross standings.

"I had a good year, and to have a factory team look in my direction and reach out is rewarding," Savatgy said. "Considering the last few years haven't been the greatest for me, I think we showed a lot this year and proved that, with the right team around me, we're able to achieve good results."

Team management framed the signing as a foundation-building step. "He has demonstrated proven results in the 450 class, showcasing impressive speed, strength, and consistency in Supercross last season," said Wisenor.

articles.title: Washington WBB's biggest stars named to Naismith Trophy watchlist
articles.summary: Washington Huskies guards Sayvia Sellers and Avery Howell were among the 50 women named to the Naismith Trophy preseason watchlist.
articles.body:
Tina Langley's backcourt headliners are both on the Naismith Trophy Women's College Player of the Year watchlist, released Thursday.

Washington guards Sayvia Sellers and Avery Howell both made the 50-woman watchlist, one of 12 sets of teammates to be featured on the list. Sellers and Howell were also the Huskies' representatives at Big Ten Media Day earlier this month and are expected to be the top two contributors for a Washington squad with real NCAA Tournament aspirations entering Langley's sixth season at the helm.

It's the second preseason watchlist of the week for Howell, who also landed on the Ann Meyers Drysdale Award watchlist as one of the best shooting guards in the country. The third-year guard was an All-Big Ten honorable mention last season after averaging 14.5 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting 43.6 percent from three-point range. Howell was also the first guard to lead the Big Ten in defensive rebounds, with 7.8 per game, since the 2022-23 season.

Sellers was the only Husky to outscore Howell last season, averaging 18 points, 3.9 assists, and 2.9 rebounds while also finishing second on the team with 25 blocks despite her 5-foot-7 stature. She was recognized as a regional finalist for the WBCA Coaches' All-America Team and made the Naismith Women's College Player of the Year Late-Season Team, the first Huskies basketball player to do either since Kelsey Plum. Sellers, now a fourth-year, also earned a spot on the All-Big Ten First Team and scored 594 points last year, the eighth-most in a single season in program history.

With both women and second-year forward Brynn McGaughy, a former five-star recruit and Big Ten All-Freshman selection last season, returning to Montlake, Langley's team would already be expected to make some noise in March. The Huskies also went out and signed 6-foot-6 third-year center Tilda Trygger, a former ACC All-Freshman honoree, from North Carolina State, 17-point scorer Brooke Carlson from Colorado State, former five-star forward Kaelyn Carroll from Kentucky, and sharpshooter Macey Huard from Oklahoma State to build out the roster and take a team that won a tournament game to the next level.

Washington enters the season ranked No. 16 in the preseason AP poll, which would give them the final right to host an NCAA Tournament regional. It's a brutal schedule, however, with 12 Big Ten foes joining Sellers and Howell on Thursday's watchlist. Four teams - No. 3 USC, led by the returning JuJu Watkins, No. 5 Michigan, No. 10 Iowa, and No. 11 UCLA - in the conference are ranked ahead of the Huskies and another four - No. 17 Minnesota, No. 18 Ohio State, No. 20 Maryland, and No. 23 Illinois - are right behind them. Only Minnesota did not have at least one player on the national watchlist released Thursday, but Nebraska, who received the most votes of an unranked team, has third-year guard Britt Prince on the list. Prince hit a three with seven seconds remaining in Alaska Airlines Arena in February to take down the Huskies, 66-65.

The Huskies start their season on Monday against UC San Diego at 11:00 a.m. PT in Alaska Airlines Arena.

articles.title: Florida State to host elite in-state 2028 OT this weekend
articles.summary: 2028 four-star offensive tackle Jackson Snelling will visit Florida State this weekend when they take on Clemson.
articles.body:
Florida State needs to land some offensive linemen in the next two recruiting cycles, as they're without one in each. As far as 2028 goes, four-star offensive tackle Jackson Snelling is a recruit they've been after heavily since the spring.

He got an offer from FSU during an unofficial visit in April, and then he returned for a camp in June. As the Seminoles get set to take on the Clemson Tigers this weekend in Tallahassee, Snelling will be one of the many recruits on campus.

He explained why he keeps coming back to see Florida State.

"I'll definitely say the relationship I have with the coaches with coach Hand, coach Manrey, coach Norvell. Definitely a top Florida school that I've been consistent with and have great a relationship with," Snelling told Chad Simmons of Rivals.

The Florida Gators are the other top contender within the state of Florida for Snelling, and he took an unofficial visit to see them last Month. He also has offers from the UCF Knights, USF Bulls, and the Florida International Panthers.

Snelling is the nation's No. 193 prospect and the No. 17 offensive tackle per Rivals industry rankings. He's also the No. 22 recruit in Florida.

The Cardinal Mooney High Star would be a great addition to FSU's 2028 class, which currently ranks No. 6 in the country .

articles.title: Falcons’ Kevin Stefanski announces James Pearce Jr.’s expected return from suspension
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons have a big divisional game on tap against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, and have been missing linebacker James Pearce Jr. after an...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have a big divisional game on tap against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, and have been missing linebacker James Pearce Jr . after an eight-game suspension handed down earlier this year. The Falcons' offense picked up the slack in a 29-20 win over the 49ers last week that led to a Jessie Bates endorsement of QB Michael Penix Jr. , but Pearce Jr. could still help in many ways.

Week 9 will bring a home game against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, a game coach Kevin Stefanski said could mark the return of Pearce Jr. to defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's group.

"Stefanski said the plan is for James Pearce Jr. to play next week," reporter Marc Raimondi said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Pearce Jr. was a 2025 first round pick of Atlanta out of the University of Tennessee who has terrorized opposing quarterbacks when he's gotten on the field. He had 10.5 sacks last season with 26 tackles. He is also talented in pass coverage, recording five pass break-ups last season.

Pearce Jr. was arrested after a domestic violence situation stemming from his relationship with WNBA star Rickea Jackson . He has not played this season after his suspension was given, but could be back on the field soon for Stefanski's team, which is tied with the Carolina Panthers at 3-4 in the NFC South, 1/2 game ahead of the New Orleans Saints and Buccaneers.

The Buccaneers are the only team that has scored more points than they've given up in the division, which lends itself to a challenge this week that the Falcons will have to navigate without Pearce Jr.'s services.

articles.title: Ravens get Lamar Jackson back but lose 2 players for Bills game
articles.summary: Ravens guard Vega Ioane and safety Jaylinn Hawkins are out against Buffalo, while Lamar Jackson has no game designation after practicing fully Friday
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without starting right guard Vega Ioane and safety Jaylinn Hawkins for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills , but quarterback Lamar Jackson is set to return after missing three consecutive games.

Baltimore released its final injury report Friday, ruling out Ioane and Hawkins while listing running back Adam Randall and cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. as questionable. Jackson carries no game-status designation after practicing fully Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

Ioane's absence is particularly notable after the rookie first-round pick returned to practice Thursday, just four days after suffering a reported MCL sprain during Baltimore's 35-13 loss to Cincinnati.

The former Penn State standout was limited Thursday and Friday, but the Ravens ultimately determined he would not be available against Buffalo.

His absence will force another adjustment along Baltimore's offensive line, which has struggled to consistently create running lanes for Derrick Henry. Emery Jones Jr. replaced Ioane against Cincinnati, while Andrew Vorhees provides another option along the interior.

Henry was limited to 45 rushing yards against the Bengals , and improving the ground game will be critical against a Buffalo offense averaging an NFL-best 32.8 points per game.

Hawkins was also ruled out after missing all three practices with a knee injury. His absence could affect Baltimore's safety rotation, although Kyle Hamilton returned to full participation Friday after being limited Thursday.

Linebacker Roquan Smith also practiced fully Friday after being limited Thursday with a knee injury, giving Baltimore two important defensive contributors ahead of its matchup against Josh Allen.

The most encouraging development involves Jackson, who is expected to reclaim his starting role after missing three games with a high ankle sprain.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism Friday about Jackson's availability, saying the team expected to have its franchise quarterback against Buffalo.

Jackson's return would provide a significant boost to an offense that has failed to score in the second half of its past two games. Baltimore has lost consecutive AFC North contests, falling to 4-3 after opening the season with four wins in five games.

Elsewhere, John Simpson practiced fully Friday despite dealing with a groin injury, while Ronnie Stanley did not participate for reasons that included scheduled rest. Neither offensive lineman received a game designation.

Randall and Tampa remain questionable while working through their designated return-to-practice windows from injured reserve. Their availability would also require roster activation.

The Ravens will finalize their active roster before Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium.

Ravens' final Week 8 injury designations

Calais Campbell (rest), Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle)

Mark Andrews, Kyle Hamilton, Trey Hendrickson, Matthew Hibner, Lamar Jackson, John Jenkins, Adam Randall, John Simpson, Roquan Smith, T.J. Tampa Jr., Broderick Washington

Randall and Tampa remain on injured reserve with return-to-practice designations. Practice participation alone does not activate them.

articles.title: Trail Blazers receive bad news on Ja Morant after injury in Grizzlies game
articles.summary: Ja Morant's injury against Memphis raises fresh concerns for Portland's season.
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers will be without Ja Morant for at least four weeks after the guard suffered a significant hamstring injury against the Memphis Grizzlies .

ESPN's NBA insider Shams Charania reported Friday that Morant sustained a Grade 2 left hamstring strain. The diagnosis delivers a major setback for Portland after its encouraging start to the 2026-27 season.

"Portland Trail Blazers' Ja Morant has sustained a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will miss at least four weeks, sources tell ESPN," Charania shared on X.

Morant suffered the injury Thursday night at Moda Center while facing his former team. He exited with 7:46 remaining after feeling discomfort while stepping back on defense.

Earlier, while speaking to the media, Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori had mentioned that Morant felt a twinge before leaving the game.

"He felt a twinge…" Nori said after the loss, while adding about the level of concern, saying, "I don't really know because this is the first time I've been around him when he's felt something. … There's always concern, but I'm hoping it's nothing major, obviously."

Portland faces early test without Ja Morant

Despite the early exit, Morant finished with 14 points and three assists in 23 minutes. Memphis eventually secured a 124-103 victory, handing Portland another difficult result.

The injury interrupts a promising beginning to Morant's Portland career. He averaged 15.8 points and 5.5 assists across his first four appearances.

His arrival had given Portland another playmaker capable of creating scoring opportunities and pushing the offense. Losing him for at least four weeks leaves the coaching staff with an important adjustment.

Portland has started the season 3-1, including Thursday's defeat. The team must now find consistent offensive production without its new starting guard.

The immediate priority will be managing Morant's recovery carefully. A Grade 2 hamstring strain can require additional rehabilitation beyond the initial absence. The Trail Blazers will reevaluate Morant in four weeks. His return will depend on his recovery progress and medical assessment.
